Week 6: Program evaluation and closing.
: The life skills workshop group-"Lifestyle Management and Well-being Workshop" — Week 1: Introduction, defining group dynamics. Week 2: Physiological Relaxation (Progressive Relaxation Exercises) Week 3: Sleep Hygiene: Circadian Rhythm and Biological Clock, Melatonin and Light Relationship, Sleep Stages and Restorative Effect Week 4: Nutrition and Stress: The effect of nutrition on stress and anxiety will be discussed: Blood Sugar Balance and "False Anxiety" (Glycemic Index), Gut-Brain Axis and Serotonin, Caffeine and Cortisol Interaction.

Week 5: Social Support and Problem Solving: Time Management and Academic Stress (Problem-Oriented Coping), Social Support and Oxytocin Effect, and Recreation and "Active Rest".

Week 6: Program evaluation and closing.

: EMG-Biofeedback — The EMG-Biofeedback program will include relaxation-based video games to reduce muscle activation. Each muscle will receive 5 minutes of application.

## NCT07607691
Evaluation of the Analgesic Efficacy and Functional Outcomes of Ultrasound-Guided PENG Block in Chronic Shoulder Pain

Intervention: : Lidocaine and Dexamethasone for PENG Block — An ultrasound-guided Pericapsular Nerve Group (PENG) block is administered to target the articular (sensory) branches of the nerves innervating the shoulder joint capsule (suprascapular, axillary, and lateral pectoral nerves) without affecting the motor branches.

The intervention is performed under strict sterile conditions with the patient in the supine position. The affected shoulder is placed in abduction and external rotation. A high-frequency ultrasound transducer is positioned parallel to the clavicle to visualize the anatomical structures. Under direct ultrasound guidance, a block needle is advanced beneath the subscapularis muscle. After confirming the correct needle positioning and ensuring no intravascular placement, a therapeutic mixture of 5 mL of 2% lidocaine and 8 mg of dexamethasone is injected into the periarticular nerve endpoints.
Link: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07607691

SUMMARY:

## NCT07801703
Optimizing the Synergy Between Behavioural Activation Therapy and Intravenous Ketamine for Treatment-Resistant Depression

Intervention: : Ketamine (0.5 mg/kg) — IV ketamine will be administered under medical supervision at a fixed dose of 0.5 mg/kg infused over 40 minutes. Treatments will be administered twice weekly for three weeks during the Induction Phase (6 treatments). Participants' response to ketamine will be assessed after the Induction Phase. Those who do not meet response criteria (\<50% reduction in MADRS score) will be deemed Nonresponders and will conclude receiving ketamine at that time. Those who meet the response criteria (≥50% reduction in MADRS score) will be deemed Responders and will proceed to the Maintenance Phase. During the Maintenance Phase, ketamine treatments will be administered once weekly for 8 weeks (8 treatments), followed by once biweekly for four weeks during the Discharge Preparation Phase (2 treatments). Responders will receive a total of 16 ketamine infusions over 15 weeks.
: Behavioural Activation Therapy — BA therapy is a structured, primarily talk therapy that focuses on helping people with depression increase engagement in positive, meaningful activities and reduce avoidance behaviors that reinforce low mood. The BA therapy protocol will be based on the approach described by Martell et al. (2022). Therapy sessions will be delivered virtually or in person according to participant preference. Participants in Arm 1 will receive a total of 16 BA sessions at a frequency of twice weekly for 3 weeks during the Induction Phase (6 sessions), once weekly for 8 weeks during the Maintenance Phase (8 sessions), and once biweekly for 4 weeks during the Discharge Preparation Phase (2 sessions). BA therapy sessions can occur on the same day as ketamine infusions, but not during or after the infusion.

## NCT07836166
Effectiveness of Noninvasive High Frequency Oscillatory Ventilation Versus Nasal Intermittent Mandatory Ventilation as Post Extubation Respiratory Support in Neonates Born At ≥ 26 Weeks' Gestation: A Randomized Clinical Trial

Intervention: : Noninvasive High Frequency Oscillatory Ventilation — nHFOV will begin immediately after planned extubation and will be delivered through binasal prongs or a nasal mask. Initial mean airway pressure will be 10-12 cm H₂O and may be increased in 1 cm H₂O steps to a maximum of 20 cm H₂O. Initial amplitude will be 15-25 cm H₂O and may be increased in 5 cm H₂O steps to a maximum of 35 cm H₂O. Frequency will be 8-12 Hz, and the inspiratory to expiratory ratio will be 1:1. Oxygen will be adjusted to maintain oxygen saturation between 90% and 95%. Settings will be adjusted according to the participant's clinical condition.
: Nasal Intermittent Mandatory Ventilation — NIMV will begin immediately after planned extubation and will be delivered through binasal prongs or a nasal mask. Positive end expiratory pressure will be 8-12 cm H₂O, and peak inspiratory pressure will be 18-24 cm H₂O. The initial breathing rate will be 30 breaths per minute and may be increased in steps of 5 to a maximum of 50 breaths per minute according to carbon dioxide levels and clinical assessment. Inspiratory time will be 0.5 seconds. Oxygen will be adjusted to maintain oxygen saturation between 90% and 95%. Synchronization will not be used.

It comprises eight individual sessions of approximately 50 minutes, delivered once weekly. Treatment focuses on crisis management, development of an individualized crisis response plan, reasons for living, relaxation, sleep management, behavioral activation, cognitive restructuring, mindfulness, coping with high-risk situations, and relapse prevention. V-BCBT is provided in addition to treatment as usual (TAU), which consists of routine outpatient psychiatric care such as pharmacotherapy and supportive psychotherapy according to clinical need.
: Treatment as Usual (TAU) — Treatment as usual (TAU) refers to routine outpatient psychiatric care provided according to each participant's clinical needs and the treating clinician's judgment. It may include pharmacotherapy, supportive psychotherapy, clinical monitoring, and other standard psychiatric services ordinarily available in outpatient practice. The specific components and intensity of TAU are not standardized by the study protocol and may vary across participants based on usual clinical care.

## NCT07924579
The Effectiveness of a Balance Exergame Intervention on Cortical Excitability/Inhibition and Functional Performance in Elderly Fallers: A Nonblinded Randomized Controlled Trial

Intervention: : Nintendo Wii Fit Balance Exergame Training — An 8-week structured balance exergame training program using the Nintendo Wii Fit platform and balance board. Participants perform barefoot multidirectional weight-shifting exercises using five available games: Ski Slalom, Table Tilt, Tightrope Tension, Balance Bubble, and Penguin Slide. Participants may choose any available game during each session. Each supervised 60-minute session consists of a 5-minute lower-limb stretching warm-up, 50 minutes of balance exergame training, and a 5-minute cool-down with stretching exercises. Training is conducted three times per week for eight weeks. A researcher oversees the intervention, and participants may take breaks as needed.
: Conventional Balance Training — An 8-week structured conventional balance training program consisting of supervised 60-minute sessions, three times per week. Each session includes a 5-minute warm-up with lower-limb stretching, 50 minutes of balance training, and a 5-minute cool-down. The balance training comprises three components: (1) Sitting balance training (15-20 minutes), including sitting on a Swiss ball to maintain balance, moving the arms or legs, throwing and catching a ball, and kicking a ball; (2) Standing balance training (15-20 minutes), including standing with feet together, shifting body weight side to side, standing on one leg, throwing and catching a ball, and standing on a foam pad or cushion; and (3) Walking training (15-20 minutes), including marching in place, walking lunges, zigzag walking, obstacle navigation, walking on a foam pad, cognitive dual-task walking, and walking while carrying a tray of water. Training intensity is adjusted according to each participant's capability.
Link: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07924579

Sleep-Stage Acoustic Stimulation for Cognitive Improvement in Alzheimer's Disease: A Randomized Sham-Controlled Study

The system uses a closed-loop design: a familiar, comfortable sound is triggered upon entry into NREM sleep, each stimulation lasts 30 seconds, with a 1-minute interval, and the number of stimulations is unlimited. In the experimental arm, the sounds are paired with a prior memory encoding task. In the active comparator arm, the sounds are unpaired (not presented during the encoding task), but all other acoustic parameters and NREM-triggered delivery remain identical. This distinguishes the intervention from standard acoustic stimulation or non-closed-loop auditory stimulation used in other studies.

## NCT07924813
Effects of Functional Electrical Stimulation Combined With Task-Oriented Training on Lower Limb Function, Balance, and Quality of Life in Children With Spastic Diplegic Cerebral Palsy.

Intervention: : Functional Electrical Stimulation Combined with Task- Oriented Training (FES+TOT) — Participants will receive Functional Electrical Stimulation combined with Task-Oriented Training for six weeks, with three supervised sessions per week (18 sessions in total, 60 minutes each). FES will be applied to the gluteus medius, Hamstring, quadriceps muscle using a frequency of 35 Hz, a pulse width of 250 μs, a ramp time of 1-2 seconds, and an on-to-off ratio of 1:3. Stimulation intensity will be adjusted to produce a visible, comfortable muscle contraction. Task-oriented training will include progressive functional activities such as sit-to-stand practice, standing weight shifting, level walking, stepping, obstacle negotiation, step-ups, stair training, and advanced gait activities.
: Task-Oriented Training (TOT) — Participants will receive Task-Oriented Training for six weeks, with three supervised sessions per week (18 sessions in total, 60 minutes each). Training will involve progressive, goal-directed functional activities to improve gross motor function, balance, and functional mobility. Activities will progress from sit-to-stand practice, standing weight shifting, and level walking to multidirectional stepping, obstacle crossing, step-ups, stair negotiation, changes in walking direction, variations in walking speed, and advanced gait activities according to participants' abilities.

## NCT07924917
Closed-Loop Bio-Machine Interaction System and Applications in Psychiatric Diagnosis and Treatment

Intervention: : Single-target active temporally interfering electrical stimulation — Single-target active stimulation targeting the right primary auditory cortex (A1), each target stimulation phase will last 20 minutes, including a 30-second ramp-up at onset and a 30-second ramp-down at termination. Alternating currents with frequencies of f1 = 2000 Hz and f2 = 2040 Hz will be delivered through the two electrode pairs, and the total current intensity across the two electrode pairs will be fixed at 4 mA (AC, peak-to-base). The intervention will be administered over two consecutive weeks, with participants receiving stimulation on five days per week.
: Dual-target active temporally interfering electrical stimulation — Dual-target active stimulation targeting the right A1 and the right dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (DLPFC), each target stimulation phase will last 20 minutes, including a 30-second ramp-up at onset and a 30-second ramp-down at termination. For each target, two pairs of electrodes will be used; the alternating current frequency and total stimulation intensity will be the same as those in the single-target active TI electrical stimulation group.The intervention will be administered over two consecutive weeks, with participants receiving stimulation on five days per week.
: Sham temporally interfering electrical stimulation — Sham TI electrical stimulation group will follow the same session duration, treatment frequency, and procedural setup as the active stimulation groups. However, electrical stimulation will be limited to an initial 30-second ramp-up followed immediately by a 30-second ramp-down, after which no current will be delivered for the remainder of the session.

## NCT07925073
Effectiveness of Low FODMAPs Diet Compared With Standard Dietary Advice in Functional Dyspepsia

Intervention: : Low Fodmap dietary advice — Participants assigned to the intervention arm will receive standard dietary advice for functional dyspepsia plus structured low-FODMAP dietary counseling provided by a registered dietitian. The intervention will last 2 weeks and will focus on reducing dietary intake of fermentable oligosaccharides, disaccharides, monosaccharides, and polyols (FODMAPs). Participants will receive verbal and written dietary guidance and will record their food intake throughout the intervention. Dietary adherence will be assessed by comparing estimated daily FODMAP intake during the intervention with baseline intake. Participants will complete weekly PAGI-SYM assessments and record bowel movements and any adverse effects.
: Standard dietary advice — Participants assigned to the control group will receive standardized verbal and written dietary advice for functional dyspepsia provided by a physician. They will not receive specific low-FODMAP dietary counseling and will continue their usual diet while following the general dietary recommendations. The intervention will last 2 weeks. Participants will complete weekly PAGI-SYM assessments and record their food intake, bowel movements, and any adverse effects during the study period
Link: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07925073

## NCT07925307
C2001P-CS6 CASCADE: A Feasibility Study of HPV Screening and Management Strategies Utilizing Extended Molecular HPV DNA Genotyping and HPV Viral Load in Women Living With HIV

Intervention: : HPV DNA Testing (Abbott Alinity m HPV Assay) — Women will self-collect a vaginal specimen for primary HPV testing to be evaluated on the Abbott Alinity m platform. The Alinity m HR HPV assay is a qualitative, real-time polymerase chain reaction (PCR) assay for the detection of high-risk HPV DNA. The assay detects 14 hrHPV genotypes by targeting the conserved L1 region of HPV DNA and provides individual or group-level genotyping results, including separate readouts for HPV 16, HPV 18, and HPV 45, and grouped detection of other high-risk types. The assay also provides a proxy for HPV viral load as measured by the cycle threshold (CT) value for the type- or group-specific readout.
: Visual Inspection with Acetic Acid — Participants with hrHPV detected will undergo visual inspection with acetic acid (VIA) during a speculum examination. Standard acetic acid (3-5%) is applied to the cervix, and the provider will assess for the presence of cervical lesions, determine suitability for ablative treatment, and characterize the transformation zone (TZ1, TZ2, or TZ3). VIA findings will be used to guide participant management and treatment decisions.
: Cervical Histology (Biopsy Procedures) — Cervical histology specimens will be obtained from participants with hrHPV detected. Biopsies may include lesion-directed cervical punch biopsies, endo- and ectocervical soft-brush biopsies, or endocervical curettage (ECC). At least two biopsies will be obtained even if no lesions are seen. For participants undergoing LEEP/LLETZ, histology will be obtained through the excisional procedure. Cervical histology will be processed locally and interpreted according to the lower anogenital squamous terminology (LAST), including p16 testing where available to confirm morphologic-appearing CIN 2.
: Cervical Treatment (Thermal Ablation or LEEP/LLETZ) — Women with HPV 16 and/or 18 will undergo immediate treatment. Women with non-16/18 hrHPV will undergo immediate treatment if cervical lesions are seen on VIA. Women who are not treated but are subsequently found to have cervical high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesions (hHSIL) on histology will return for cervical treatment. Treatment modality will be determined based on the extent of cervical lesions, with thermal ablation (TA) used for lesions appropriate for ablative therapy and LEEP/LLETZ used for more extensive lesions.
Link: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07925307

SUMMARY:

## NCT05911529
Tracking the Linguistic Signatures of Motivational Interviewing in Acute Psychosis (Former: Motivational Interviewing for Patients With Acute Psychosis)

Intervention: : Motivational Interviewing — In our study intervention, patients should receive three session of motivational interviewing (MI). Throughout the MI sessions, interviewers use common MI techniques including open-ended questions, affirmations, reflections, summaries, asking permission, expressing empathy, supporting self-efficacy, etc. Interviewers are clinical psychologists who received MI training immediately prior to the study.
: Psychoeducation — In the control intervention patients should also be given three sessions, in which no MI techniques take place. They will be carried out in the form of psychoeducational interventions, which are part of a standard treatment program for patients with schizophrenia during the acute and post-acute phases. Psychoeducation aims to inform patients about their illness and its treatment, enhancing both the understanding and the personally responsible handling of the illness and supporting those afflicted in coping with the disorder. Since we want to check whether the patients really benefit from the specific intervention rather than from receiving additional contact time, the patient in the control group will also be given three sessions. It is known that psychoeducation can have a positive effect on treatment out come by reducing relapse rate and the frequency of rehospitalizations, improving treatment ad herence, and shortening the length of inpatient hospital stays.
Link: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT05911529

## NCT06445049
Assessing Intrinsic Respiratory Rate in Mechanically Ventilated Adult Patients With Reverse Triggering as an Incentive for Accelerating Transition to Spontaneous Breathing and Extubation: Pilot Randomized Clinical Trial - INTRINSIC

Intervention: : brief test — The intervention is a simple brief test as follows: With the ventilator set with the patient clinical settings, it will be performed an up to 30sec-long or two inspiratory effort and-expiratory occlusion maneuver on the ventilator and/or switch the patient to pressure support for up to 30sec-long to assess the presence of intrinsic respiratory rate.

If an intrinsic respiratory rate ≥8 breaths per minute is present and P/F ratio is ≥150 it will be performed a 5-minute "test" in pressure support ventilation with the pressure support level to match the clinical setting of the patient. If the patient tolerates well 5 minutes in pressure support (see criteria below) the clinical team will be informed:

\- It will be indicated that the patient tolerated 5 min of PSV and suggest to the clinicians and physician in charge to transition the patient to pressure support ventilation plus suggest reducing sedation.

The de-epithelialized graft (CTG) will be sutured in position, at the level of the cement-enamel junction (CEJ), using interrupted absorbable sutures. ## NCT07579988
Ultrasound Measurement of Thyroid Volume in Term Newborns : a Single-centre Cross Sectional Observational Study

Intervention: : Thyroid ultrasound — Thyroid Ultrasound is a safe method because it does not involve ionizing radiation, is non-invasive and painless, takes only a few minutes, and does not cause discomfort. The Ultrasound machine is the Philips EPIQ 5 system (Philips Healthcare, Eindhoven, the Netherlands) with CE certification. The examination is conducted with high-frequency probes (linear hockey stick L12-20 MHz). All thyroid gland scans and measurements are performed by two trained observers at the bedside using a portable scanner. A generous amount of coupling gel is applied to the transducer surface, which is placed midline on the neck of the infant. The examination of each lobe is performed in both longitudinal and transverse projections. During the examination, the neonate is in the supine position with slight extension of the neck, while sucking on an assistant's gloved finger with glucose drops.

## NCT07621978
Feasibility and Potential Efficacy of High-intensity Gait Training in Individuals With Cerebellar Damage

Intervention: : High-intensity training in variable contexts — High intensity stepping training: Training sessions will focus on maximizing stepping activities in variable contexts while targeting ≥70% HR reserve (or approximately 80% age-predicted maximum HR) calculated using the Karvonen formula. Target HR will be decreased by 10 beats if the individual is on beta-blockers. Intensity will also be monitored using the Borg RPE scale every 3-5 minutes with goals of ≥15 on a 6-20 scale. The intensity of the walking training will be primarily modulated through the treadmill speed and incline as well as addition of weights to the torso or limbs for the purpose of error augmentation and not to dampen ataxia. Sessions will focus on achieving up to 40 minutes of stepping training within each 60-minute session. Potential tasks include walking in multiple directions, over inclines and obstacles, and/or with weighted vests and leg weights with limited handrail use as tolerated and decided by the therapist and participant.
: Conventional balance training — Conventional training: Training sessions will focus on improving static and dynamic balance, while calculated using the Karvonen formula. Target HR ranges will be decreased by 10 beats if the individual is on beta-blockers. Intensity will also be monitored using heart rates and RPE every 3-5 minutes with goals of \<14 on a 6-20 scale. Sessions will focus on balance training for up to 40 minutes within a 60-minute session. Individuals will perform \~10 minutes (\~25% of sessions) on balance activities in the sitting position, \~20 minutes (50% of sessions) of standing positions and \~10 minutes (25% of sessions) of walking training.
Link: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07621978

SUMMARY:

## NCT07741396
BRIDGE Trial: Embedding Consumer-grade mHealth Technologies Into Cardiac Rehabilitation as a Model for Chronic Disease Management

Intervention: : CBCR — The CBCR program at UI Health is a structured, medically supervised secondary prevention program for patients with qualifying cardiovascular conditions. It includes individualized aerobic and resistance exercise training, clinical monitoring during exercise sessions, education on heart disease and risk factor management, counseling to promote healthy lifestyle behaviors, and support for long-term adherence to prescribed treatment and self-care recommendations. Participants are encouraged to attend up to 36 supervised sessions over \~12 weeks.
: BRIDGE mHealth intervention — Description: The intervention includes three commercially available mHealth apps and devices: Withings Body Composition weight scale, Withings BP monitor, and Fitbit Charge 6 activity tracker along with their companion mobile apps. Each app incorporates behavior change tools that support daily self-monitoring, feedback, and reminders across key cardiac rehabilitation domains, including physical activity, weight and blood pressure management, and cardiovascular risk factor reduction. Participants will also receive up to five individually tailored text messages per week throughout the intervention period. Messages will be individualized based on (1) patient responses to validated questionnaires administered at baseline and (2) patient-generated health data from the app/devices. Messages will target physical activity, healthy eating, weight management, blood pressure control, and cardiovascular risk reduction.

## NCT07787559
Efficacy of the Epley Versus Semont-plus Maneuver in Patients With Posterior Semicircular Canal Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo: A Randomized Controlled Trial Using Quantitative Video-Nystagmography Measurement

Intervention: : Semont-plus — Semont-plus liberatory maneuver for posterior canal BPPV, performed by a trained therapist at the enrolment visit. From the upright seated position the head is turned 45 degrees toward the nonaffected side. The body is then moved 150 degrees toward the affected side, so that the head comes to lie about 60 degrees below the earth horizontal and the otoconia are carried beyond the vertex of the canal. The body is next moved 240 degrees toward the nonaffected side, which drives the otoconia toward the vestibule, and the participant is finally brought 90 degrees back to the upright position. Each position is held for about one minute or until the induced nystagmus stops. The maneuver is repeated within the same session if positional nystagmus persists. Participants are then taught to perform it on their own at home, as often as they are able, and to record each home session in a diary.
: Epley — Epley maneuver for posterior canal BPPV, performed by a trained therapist at the enrolment visit. From the upright seated position the head is rotated 45 degrees toward the affected ear. The body is then moved backward so that the head hangs below the earth horizontal. The head is rotated 90 degrees toward the nonaffected ear, after which the whole body is rotated downward until the participant faces the floor with the affected ear pointing toward the ceiling. The participant returns to sitting with the head still rotated 45 degrees toward the nonaffected ear, and the head is turned back to neutral at the end. Each position is held until the induced nystagmus stops, and for at least 30 seconds. The maneuver is repeated within the same session if positional nystagmus persists. Participants are then taught to perform it on their own at home, as often as they are able, and to record each home session in a diary.
Link: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07787559

## NCT07822828
A Mechanism Randomised Controlled Trial of a Three-Agent LLM-Augmented mHealth Intervention for Late-Life Loneliness in Older Adults

Intervention: : Hybrid conversational companion application — Companion responses are generated by a large language model through the official DeepSeek API, accessed via Firebase Cloud Functions. The model version is not fixed, so the model identifier returned with each response is logged. Responses are conditioned on the companion's system prompt, conversation history, cross-session memory, and the current input. In reminiscence, the model asks one follow-up question after each answer, and at the end of each week a DeepSeek model drafts a short life-story chapter that a second model checks against the conversation. Four in-app tools (Action Loop, Thought Exercise, Education, Progress). Five LLM-distinctive behaviours are tagged in logs as a cumulative within-arm exposure variable. Conversational text is sent to the model provider; participants are advised not to include identifying information. Participants are encouraged to use the app daily and at least five times per week for four weeks; use is not mandatory and is logged.
: Rule-based conversational companion application — Identical interface, navigation, companion names and personae, tool layer, notification schedule, and in-app assessment prompts. Replies are assembled from pre-written templates by keyword matching and conversational state; no language model is used. In free conversation, Siu Yan's replies are drawn in rotation from a pool of pre-written sentences. The daily check-in is a short conversation with fixed questions, followed by a pre-written response chosen by the participant's answer. In reminiscence, both arms use the same open questions; in this arm each answer is followed by a fixed acknowledgement, and the participant's own answers are arranged, unchanged, into a weekly life-story chapter. No cross-session memory. Conversational content is not sent to any external service; a local safety classifier, hosted by the research team, is used in both arms. Attention- and interface-matched active comparator. Recommended use, expected daily duration, and logging are identical to the experiment
Link: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07822828

## NCT07829107
Comparing the Effectiveness of a Biomarker-plus-clinical Guidelines Algorithm Versus Clinical Guidelines Only for Safely Decreasing Brain Computed Tomography Utilization During Brain Injury Evaluations: The PIONEER Comparative Effectiveness Study

Intervention: : Clinical pathway 1: Guidelines plus biomarkers — Patients will be managed using an algorithm that integrates the Canadian CT Head Rule (CCHR) with i-STAT whole-blood GFAP and UCH-L1 testing. Patients who meet CCHR criteria for CT imaging and those whose CT imaging decision-making is not covered by CCHR (e.g., no loss of consciousness or amnesia) will receive i-STAT testing. Sites will be assigned to one of three implementation waves, with two sites transitioning to the Guidelines + Biomarkers phase every six months. Prior to their assigned transition, sites will continue to use guidelines alone. Once a site transitions to the Guidelines + Biomarkers phase, the integrated biomarker-guided algorithm will become the standard-of-care protocol at that site for eligible patients and will remain the standard of care for the remainder of the study.
: Clinical guidelines only — During the baseline phase, sites will rely solely on established clinical guidelines to guide brain CT utilization in patients with suspected TBI. Specifically, providers will apply the Canadian CT Head Rule, a validated decision instrument that identifies patients at high risk for clinically important brain injury who require CT imaging. All sites will begin in this Guidelines-Only baseline phase and will continue using this approach until their assigned transition to the Guidelines + Biomarkers phase. Sites will transition in three waves, with two sites transitioning every six months.
Link: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07829107

## NCT07872384
Improving Functional Recovery in Skilled Nursing Facilities Through Supplemental Mobility

Intervention: : High Intensity Rehabilitation — An 8RM is the dose necessary for most effective strength gains in community-dwelling older adults, and is equivalent to 80% of a one repetition max, which is the maximal load needed to voluntarily complete one repetition of a given exercise with proper form. Activities will include strength training, transfer practice, balance training, advanced ADLs. Clinicians will tailor the intervention for each activity to target overload using 8-repetition maximum for resistance training. Other interventions will be performed to muscle failure or inability to complete the final repetition. Failure is the inability to complete a repetition through the full, available range of motion without significant compensation. Further, high-intensity dosing requires continuous, volitional effort from the patient; therefore, incorporation of motivational interviewing strategies across sessions will maximize patient effort and self-efficacy.
: Safe Transfers and Mobility Program — The Safe Transfers and Mobility Program (STAMP) embeds a mobility aide into daily care. STAMP is a patient-centered, scalable approach to extend the benefits of rehabilitation sessions by increasing mobility throughout the day and reinforcing activity between therapy sessions. Core components are: (1) targeting 45 minutes of additional daily physical activity through support with walking and functional mobility tasks; (2) establishing individualized mobility goals collaboratively set by the therapist and patient, based on functional level; (3) delivering progressive activities with walking distances increased by \~30% weekly, adjusted for patient tolerance; and (4) interdisciplinary coordination to incorporate STAMP sessions into routine care with minimal disruption to clinical workflow. Prior work suggests that 45 minutes of STAMP can at least double daily step counts, and increasing walking distance by 30% per week is feasible even for individuals with low baseline function.
: Usual Care — Usual Care SNFs will continue with routine collection and documentation of physical performance outcomes (gait speed, SPPB, Modified Barthel ADL Index) as standard practice. Importantly, the Usual Care SNF including the facility, rehabilitation clinicians, and patients will not have access to i-STRONGER materials.
Link: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07872384

## NCT07883486
Post-operative Pain and Apical Healing After Root Canal (re)Treatment With Laser-activated Irrigation Versus Sonic or no Activation: a Multi-centre Randomised Controlled Clinical Trial

Intervention: : sonically activated irrigation — The irrigant is activated after mechanical preparation with a plastic Eddy-tip (f = 6000 Hz) inserted up to 1 - 3 mm short of the working length. Three 20 s activation cycles are performed per canal, with 2 mL irrigation in each root canal between the cycles.
: laser activated irrigation — The irrigant is activated after mechanical preparation with a pulsed Er:YAG laser (Fotona Fidelis III, PIPS, E = 20 mJ, f = 20 Hz, t = 50 μs). These settings result in a power of 0.4 W. Due to the high absorption of the Er:YAG wavelength in the irrigant, mechanical effects occur (cavitation), rather than thermal effects. As a result, the risk of thermal damage is negligible. The tip of the laser is kept at the canal orifice, but not inserted into the root canal. During activation, irrigant is continuously added to the pulp chamber, so the root canals and pulp chamber are consistently immersed in irrigating solution. Three 20 s activating cycles per orifice are executed, with intermittent flushing of the root canal with 2 mL irrigant.
: conventional needle irrigation — The root canals are irrigated with 3% NaOCl, using a 27G notched needle, adapted to a 3 mL syringe and inserted up to 2 - 3 mm short of working length. Two millilitres of irrigant are used between the different instruments.
Link: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07883486

Comparison of the Effects of Optokinetic Stimulation Added to a Neuromuscular Training Program on Jump-Landing Biomechanics, Visual Dependence, and Reactive Transfer Performance

Intervention: : Neuromuscular Training — Supervised neuromuscular training will be delivered three times per week for six weeks (18 sessions), in addition to usual basketball team training. Each session will last approximately 25-30 minutes and include strength, balance, proximal control, and plyometric exercises. Exercises will progress from bilateral squats, walking lunges, single-leg balance, and drop landings to single-leg squats, drop jumps, single-leg countermovement jumps, and single-leg standing long jumps. Exercises will be performed in 3-4 sets, with 60-90 seconds of rest between sets. Exercise difficulty and repetitions will progress according to the weekly protocol.
: Virtual Reality-Based Optokinetic Stimulation — Optokinetic stimulation will be delivered using a Meta Quest 3S headset and custom Unity software immediately before neuromuscular training, three times per week for six weeks. Participants will track moving balloons with their eyes while keeping their head and trunk as still as possible. Weekly progression will be: week 1, seated, 20 degrees/s, 3 x 30 s; week 2, standing with feet together, 20 degrees/s, 3 x 60 s; week 3, semi-tandem stance, 30 degrees/s, 3 x 90 s; week 4, tandem stance, 40 degrees/s, 3 x 120 s; week 5, tandem stance, 50 degrees/s, 3 x 150 s; week 6, tandem stance, 60 degrees/s, 3 x 180 s. Clockwise and counterclockwise motion will be presented for equal durations. Background rotation speed will be twice the balloon speed. Symptoms will be monitored using the Simulator Sickness Questionnaire, with exposure adjusted according to tolerance.

Effects of Optokinetic Stimulation Added to Drop Vertical Jump Training on Landing Error Scores and Dynamic Knee Valgus: An Assessor-Blinded Randomized Controlled Trial

Intervention: : Drop Vertical Jump Training — Following a standardized warm-up and task familiarization, participants will perform two blocks of 10 drop vertical jumps from a 30-cm box toward a target positioned at 50% of their height. After landing on both feet, participants will immediately jump as high and forward as possible and maintain the final landing position for five seconds. Rest periods will be 30 seconds between repetitions and five minutes between blocks. Feedback based on real-time landing error scores will be provided after each block.
: Virtual Reality-Based Optokinetic Stimulation — Optokinetic stimulation will be delivered through a Meta Quest 3S headset while participants sit in a supported chair with their feet on the floor. Participants will track a red balloon with their eyes while keeping their head as still as possible. Foreground stimuli will move at 30 degrees per second, with the background moving in the opposite direction at twice that speed. Three 60-second exposures will be delivered in each direction before each training block, with 30-60-second rest periods. Active stimulation will total six minutes per block and 12 minutes across the session, excluding rest. The headset will be removed before jump training.
Link: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07918612

SUMMARY:

Intervention: : Laughter Yoga — Laughter yoga is a structured intervention combining simulated laughter exercises, breathing techniques, rhythmic clapping, light warm-up movements, and playful activities. Participants will attend live online group sessions via Zoom, conducted by a researcher certified in laughter yoga. The first session will include brief information about laughter yoga, its principles, and breathing techniques. Each session will last approximately 30 minutes and will consist of deep breathing exercises (10 minutes), clapping and warm-up exercises (5 minutes), playful activities (5 minutes), and laughter exercises followed by relaxation (10 minutes). The intervention will be delivered twice weekly for four weeks, comprising eight sessions in total. Participants will be organized into groups of 5 to 25 individuals. Attendance will be monitored, and reminder messages will be sent via WhatsApp and/or SMS before sessions.
: Progressive Muscle Relaxation — Progressive muscle relaxation is a structured relaxation technique involving the sequential tensing and relaxing of different muscle groups to help participants recognize and reduce muscle tension. Participants will attend live online group sessions via Zoom, guided by the researcher. The first session will include brief information about the purpose, benefits, and application steps of the technique. Participants will also receive a written and illustrated educational brochure. During sessions, participants will be guided through exercises involving the hand, arm, shoulder, face, neck, back, abdominal, hip, leg, and foot muscle groups. Each muscle group will be tensed for approximately 5-7 seconds and then relaxed for 10-15 seconds, accompanied by slow and controlled breathing. Each session will last approximately 30 minutes. The intervention will be delivered twice weekly for four weeks, comprising eight sessions in total. Participants will be organized into groups of 5 to 25 individu
Link: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07927426

## NCT07927465
Neoadjuvant Finotonlimab Plus TP Regimen in Locally Advanced INI-1 (SMARCB1)-Deficient Sinonasal Carcinoma: A Prospective, Multicenter, Single-Arm Phase II Clinical Study

Intervention: : Finotonlimab — Finotonlimab is an anti-PD-1 monoclonal antibody administered as part of neoadjuvant therapy. It is given intravenously at a fixed dose of 200 mg on day 1 of each 21-day cycle, for a total of 2 cycles. It is infused before paclitaxel and cisplatin on the same day. This is the experimental immunotherapy component of the study regimen.
: Paclitaxel — Paclitaxel is a standard cytotoxic chemotherapy agent administered as part of the neoadjuvant TP regimen. It is given by intravenous infusion over 3 hours on day 1 of each 21-day cycle, at a dose of 135-175 mg/m², for a total of 2 cycles. Standard premedication (dexamethasone, diphenhydramine, and cimetidine or an equivalent H2 blocker) is given before infusion to prevent hypersensitivity reactions. Paclitaxel is administered after finotonlimab and before cisplatin.
: Cisplatin — Cisplatin is a standard platinum-based chemotherapy agent administered as part of the neoadjuvant TP regimen. It is given by intravenous infusion at a dose of 70-75 mg/m² on days 1-3 of each 21-day cycle, with the total dose for the cycle divided across the three days, for a total of 2 cycles. It is administered after paclitaxel on day 1. Standard hydration, diuresis, and electrolyte supplementation (potassium and magnesium) are provided. This divided-day schedule is used to reduce acute nephrotoxicity and severe emesis associated with single high-dose cisplatin.
Link: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07927465

SUMMARY:

## NCT07927530
Efficacy of Ultrasound-Guided Thoracolumbar Fascia Injection in the Treatment of Chronic Low Back Pain in Patients With Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus: A Randomized Controlled Trial

Intervention: : Ultrasound-Guided Thoracolumbar Fascia Injection — A single ultrasound-guided thoracolumbar fascia injection will be performed with the patient in the prone position under aseptic conditions. Using an in-plane technique, a 22-gauge needle will be advanced into the middle layer of the thoracolumbar fascia between the quadratus lumborum and erector spinae muscles at the L4 level. Correct needle placement will be confirmed by hydrodissection using approximately 2 mL of local anesthetic. Subsequently, 10 mL of 0.25% bupivacaine and 40 mg of methylprednisolone acetate will be administered into the interfascial plane.
: Standard Conservative Treatment — Standard conservative treatment will consist of structured patient education and a home-based exercise program. The exercise program will include lumbopelvic and core stabilization exercises, abdominal and paraspinal muscle strengthening, hip muscle strengthening, lower extremity stretching, and aerobic activity as tolerated. Participants will receive instructions on correct exercise techniques, maintaining daily activities, and avoiding prolonged bed rest. The program will be recommended for regular home practice throughout the study period.
Link: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07927530

## NCT07927816
A Single-Arm, Dose-Escalation Clinical Study on the Safety of CD19 Sequential CD22 In Vivo CAR-T Cell Immunotherapy for Relapsed/Refractory B-Cell Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia

Intervention: : CD19-Targeted In Vivo CAR-T Injection (first infusion, Day 0); CD22 -Targeted In Vivo CAR-T Injection (second infusion, Day 7) — The investigational products are engineered lentiviral vector-based in vivo gene therapy products. The viral envelope receptor-binding domain has been mutated to abolish native pantropic infectivity, and a targeting module composed of an anti-CD7 nanobody (VHH) and a T/NK-cell-specific ligand (CD58 extracellular domain) has been incorporated into the envelope, enabling specific transduction of circulating T cells and NK cells in situ and expression of a chimeric antigen receptor directed against CD19 (first infusion, Day 0) or CD22 (second infusion, Day 7). No leukapheresis, ex vivo manufacturing, or lymphodepleting conditioning is required. Dose escalation follows a traditional 3+3 design with planned dose levels of 1×10\^9, 3×10\^9, and 6×10\^9 transducing units (TU), guided by the occurrence of dose-limiting toxicities (DLTs).

Participants receive the necessary equipment. Additionally, participants in the intervention group receive a consultation with a physiotherapist about their home-based exercise program, along with training on proper use of wearable devices and mobile applications.

## NCT07929090
Comparison of the Effects of Pectoral Nerve Block and Serratus Posterior Superior Intercostal Plane Block on Acute and Persistent Postoperative Pain After Mastectomy: A Prospective, Double-Blind, Randomized Controlled Trial

Intervention: : Ultrasound-Guided Serratus Posterior Superior Intercostal Plane Block — A single ultrasound-guided block will be performed on the surgical side before induction of general anesthesia. With the participant seated and the hand on the opposite shoulder, a high-frequency linear ultrasound probe will be positioned along the medial scapular border to identify the third rib and serratus posterior superior muscle. A 50-mm block needle will be advanced in-plane in a caudal-to-cranial direction. After confirming the plane with 5 mL of saline, 30 mL of 0.25% bupivacaine with epinephrine will be injected between the serratus posterior superior and intercostal muscles.
: Ultrasound-Guided Pectoral Nerve Block Type II — A single ultrasound-guided PECS II block will be performed on the surgical side before induction of general anesthesia, with the participant supine. A high-frequency linear ultrasound probe will be used to identify the pectoralis major, pectoralis minor, and serratus anterior muscles. A 50-mm block needle will be advanced using an in-plane approach. After confirming each injection plane with 5 mL of saline, 10 mL of 0.25% bupivacaine with epinephrine will be injected between pectoralis major and pectoralis minor, followed by 20 mL of the same solution between pectoralis minor and serratus anterior.
Link: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07929090

## NCT07932691
A Multicenter, Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled Phase I Study to Evaluate the Safety, Tolerability, Pharmacokinetics, and Pharmacodynamics of Single and Multiple Ascending Doses of VDJ010 for Subcutaneous Injection in Healthy Chinese Subjects and Patients With Ulcerative Colitis

Intervention: : Recombinant Human Interleukin-2 Fusion Protein with Human Serum Albumin (VDJ010) — VDJ010 is a recombinant fusion protein consisting of human interleukin-2 (IL-2) genetically fused to human serum albumin (HSA), produced using Chinese hamster ovary (CHO) cells through DNA recombinant technology. The fusion protein selectively binds to the high-affinity IL-2 receptor (IL-2Rαβγ) constitutively expressed on regulatory T cells (Treg), thereby promoting Treg expansion and restoring immune tolerance in autoimmune diseases such as ulcerative colitis. The HSA moiety extends the plasma half-life of IL-2 to enable less frequent subcutaneous dosing.
: Placebo — This is a matching placebo formulation containing no active pharmaceutical ingredient (API). The placebo is manufactured to be identical in appearance, color, shape, size, and packaging to the investigational product VDJ010 to maintain the integrity of the double-blind design. It is utilized solely as a control intervention for the purpose of this randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase I clinical trial.

## NCT06042413
Real-world and Innovative Multimodal Prediction and Prevention of Postoperative Mortality and Multi-morbidities

Intervention: : Personalized CPC Prehabilitation — Patients referred for elective surgery will be scheduled for a preoperative evaluation (3 to 6 weeks prior to surgery) and will receive standardized and personalized assessment and prehabilitation according to UPMC disease specific algorithms
: Cognitive Training — Participants will be provided with access to the Lumosity (Lumos Labs) software for installation on a home device. They will be trained to navigate the touchscreen tablet and guided through an introductory series of brain exercise games focused on 5 main categories: memory, speed, attention, flexibility, and problem-solving. Patients will be asked to complete a cognitive exercise dosage of a minimum of 20 minutes a day for ≥5 days prior to their date of surgery. Research coordinators and volunteers from UPMC's Hospital Elder Life Program (HELP) will reach out to participants daily for a quick social check-in and to remind them to perform their training. Compliance data will be retrieved from the Lumosity app.
: Meditation — A single guided meditation session with instructions will be provided using a smart device. The meditation session will last for at least 10 minutes daily starting at least 1-week prior to surgery. If the subject does not own a smart device, one will be provided or meditation will be completed in-person or over the phone.
: Daily Exercise — Participants in the intervention group will meet with an occupational or physical therapist approximately 1-6 weeks before surgery who will discuss the potential benefits of exercise and give directions for an easy strength training exercise. Participants will then be provided with a video link for a guided exercise and encouraged to walk or perform a seated strength exercise for ≥ 5 minutes each day for at least 1 week before surgery and after surgery. Patient reported frequency, fitness app compliance and exercise duration with REDCap email or mobile link or over telephone will be collected before and after surgery. Patients will be cleared by an occupational or physical therapist to perform the upper-extremity exercises and will confirm the exercises are not contraindicated after surgery. An occupational or physical therapist will see subject again post-surgery to mitigate risk of injury.
: Enhanced Social Support — Research coordinators and volunteers from the Hospital Elder Life Program (HELP) will contact participants prior to surgery to discuss concerns, provide regular social support, and remind participants to complete assigned cognitive exercises. The role of family members and caregivers in supporting the participant will also be discussed, and their involvement will be encouraged when appropriate.

Participants in the CPC preoperative intervention group may receive preoperative interventions to address depressive symptoms as part of CPC-guided prehabilitation, when clinically indicated.
: Proactive Bundle Interventions — Participants randomized to the proactive bundled intervention group (Group D) will receive routine intraoperative SSEP and EEG monitoring and proactive optimization of intraoperative physiology, including maintaining mean arterial pressure ≥65 mmHg, adequate oxygenation, opioid sparing analgesia, and avoidance of deep anesthesia and benzodiazepines.

If persistent focal changes in SSEP and EEG (i.e., changes in one hemisphere) occur, reactive measures will be implemented to increase cerebral perfusion, including ensuring hematocrit \>30, maintaining anesthetic BIS \>50-60, and initiating stroke management and thrombectomy if clinically indicated
: Pre-operative Standard of Care — Participants will receive routine preoperative clinical care per institutional standard practice.
: Intra-operative Standard of Care — This includes routine intraoperative SSEP and EEG monitoring. Physician oversight and interpretation of real-time neuromonitoring data will be performed using a combined on-site and remote model at UPMC. In the event that changes in EEG or SSEP are considered significant by the oversight neurophysiologists, the surgical team will be immediately informed so that immediate appropriate action can be taken to reverse the change.
Link: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT06042413

SUMMARY:

## NCT06282250
An Explorative and Experimental Study to Assess the Feasibility, Acceptability, and Effectiveness of Early Intervention With Light, Lifestyle and ImCT Therapy in Individuals at Risk for Bipolar Disorder

Intervention: : Bright light therapy + Psycho-education + Imagery focused Cognitive Therapy — Week 1-3: BLT will be administered for 30 minutes on five consecutive days, starting on Monday of the work week, between 7:30 AM and 10:00. The effect of the light therapy is evaluated by means of the Self-Rated Quick Inventory of Depressive Symptoms (QIDS-SR). Further treatment strategy is determined on the basis of these results:

* If the patient has achieved remission (QIDS-SR \< 6), BLT has been successful and the patient can continue with PE and IMCT.
* If there is insufficient or no response (QIDS-SR of 6 or higher), BLT is extended with five more sessions the following week.
* If necessary, a third week is optional.

Week 2-4: Psycho Education will follow, 1 session.

Week 3/4-9/10: ImCT will follow, 6 sessions.
: Blue-light blocking glasses + Psycho-education + Imagery focused Cognitive Therapy — Week 1-3: blue-light blocking glasses will be administered. Week 2-4: Psycho Education will follow, 1 session.

Week 3/4-9/10: ImCT will follow, 6 sessions.
: Psycho-education + Imagery focused Cognitive Therapy — Week 1: Psycho Education, 1 session.

Week 2-7: ImCT will follow, 6 sessions.

Scoring of the visual analog scale is based on a visual scale ranging from 0 (worst imaginable health state) to 100 (best imaginable health state). Higher scores indicate better health status. ## NCT07163299
Selective Intra-arterial Hypothermic Magnesium Sulfate Infusion in Combination With Endovascular Thrombectomy in Acute Ischemic Stroke: A Phase 1/2 Randomized Clinical Trial

Intervention: : Endovascular thrombectomy combination with selective intra-arterial hypothermic magnesium sulfate infusion (350 ml). — According to patient's weight, magnesium sulfate (MgSO4) will be diluted to 350 ml 4°C saline solution (0.6μmol/kg/ml). During the thrombectomy procedure, a micro-catheter will be advanced until it reaches beyond the clot responsible for the ischemic symptoms, then cold 50 ml MgSO4 solution will be infused into the ischemic territory at 10 ml/min through the micro-catheter. After that, thrombectomy with a stent retriever will be performed to recanalize the occluded vessel as soon as possible. Immediately after successful thrombectomy, cold MgSO4 solution will be re-infused into the ischemic brain tissue through the catheter at a rate of 30 ml/min for 10 min.

Note: The pre-planned weight-tailored magnesium solution could not be prepared intraoperatively in phase 1 due to unavailable emergency pharmacy workflow. All 9 patients received uniform 20.29 mmol/L perfusate, with only infusion volume escalated.
: Endovascular thrombectomy combination with selective intra-arterial hypothermic magnesium sulfate infusion (500 ml). — According to patient's weight, magnesium sulfate (MgSO4) will be diluted to 500 ml 4°C saline solution (0.6μmol/kg/ml). During the thrombectomy procedure, a micro-catheter will be advanced until it reaches beyond the clot responsible for the ischemic symptoms, then cold 50 ml MgSO4 solution will be infused into the ischemic territory at 10 ml/min through the micro-catheter. After that, thrombectomy with a stent retriever will be performed to recanalize the occluded vessel as soon as possible. Immediately after successful thrombectomy, cold MgSO4 solution will be re-infused into the ischemic brain tissue through the catheter at a rate of 30 ml/min for 10 min. Then pause for 5 min, followed by another 5 min of infusion at the original rate.Note: The pre-planned weight-tailored magnesium solution could not be prepared intraoperatively in phase 1 due to unavailable emergency pharmacy workflow. All 9 patients received uniform 20.29 mmol/L perfusate, with only infusion volume escalated.
: Endovascular thrombectomy combination with selective intra-arterial hypothermic magnesium sulfate infusion (650 ml). — According to patient's weight, magnesium sulfate (MgSO4) will be diluted to 650 ml 4°C saline solution (0.6μmol/kg/ml). During the thrombectomy procedure, a micro-catheter will be advanced until it reaches beyond the clot responsible for the ischemic symptoms, then cold 50 ml MgSO4 solution will be infused into the ischemic territory at 10 ml/min through the micro-catheter. After that, thrombectomy with a stent retriever will be performed to recanalize the occluded vessel as soon as possible. Immediately after successful thrombectomy, cold MgSO4 solution will be re-infused into the ischemic brain tissue through the catheter at a rate of 30 ml/min for 10 min. Then pause for 5 min, followed by intermittent infusion at the original rate for another 5 min twice. The interval between two times is also 5 min.Note: The pre-planned weight-tailored magnesium solution could not be prepared intraoperatively in phase 1.All 9 patients received uniform 20.29 mmol/L perfusate.
: Endovascular thrombectomy — Endovascular thrombectomy
: Phase 2 Fixed-Volume Concentration-Escalation Cohort — This phase 2 cohort uses a fixed 650 mL maximum infusion volume with six ascending magnesium concentrations: 20.29, 22.54, 25.36, 28.98, 33.81, 40.57 mmol/L. Each tier is mixed by diluting one 5 g magnesium stock into 1000/900/800/700/600/500 mL pre-cooled saline. After confirming safe magnesium levels, we will adopt the registry's weight-based formulation. Infusion protocols match phase 1, and this two-stage design is approved under IRB amendment No.XYFY2025-KL360-02
Link: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07163299

## NCT07168395
Pre-emptive RTO for An Early Detected Gastric Varices in CT/MR Angiogram Trial (PRADA Trial)

Intervention: : Non-selective beta blockers — Non-selective beta blockers are used in patients who have not had a previous variceal bleed to prevent bleeding by reducing blood pressure in the liver. These drugs also work by blocking beta receptors that reduce cardiac output and by causing vessel constriction in the abdominal organs, which lowers blood flow to the liver and the existing varices.
: Retrograde transvenous obliteration — Pre-emptive retrograde transvenous obliteration will be performed in patients randomized to this arm to evaluate the effectiveness in decreasing gastric variceal bleeding. Either CARTO or PARTO (coil or plug-assisted retrograde transvenous obliteration) will be performed using EMBOLIZATION COILS or VASCULAR PLUGS of different sizes based on the size of the shunt. Additionally, Gelfoam (collagen sponges) slurry will be injected into the shunt and varices to completely obliterate them.

The microspheres are trapped in the vasculature of the tumor due to arteriolar capillary blockage where they exert a local radiotherapeutic effect. In clinical use, the glass microspheres remain permanently trapped in the vasculature where the isotope decays to infinity leaving background radiation with no therapeutic value. Optimizing Referral Pathways for Patients With Hematuria and Moderate-Severe Proteinuria - Phase 2: A Quality Improvement Project

Intervention: : Electronic Health Record alert — The EHR alert will open upon logging into patient's chart. It will display relevant information about hematuria (dipstick blood), urine microscopy (if available), proteinuria (ACR, PCR, dipstick protein), most recent (if ever) nephrology visit, and most recent (if ever) urology visit. The EHR alert will provide a preselected order button for a nephrology referral with the indication pre-filled out. It will also provide options to order confirmatory urinalysis with microscopy testing and an option to refer to urology. The provider will have an option to deselect the nephrology referral, which will prompt reasons for not ordering the referral: "Not appropriate"; "already seeing a nephrologist"; "palliative care"; "patient refuses"; "Other (document)". The alert will not be a hard-stop in the chart.

Intervention: : ZE74-0282 — ZE74-0282 is an oral powder for suspension supplied in 25 mg and 75 mg sachets. It is administered orally with noncarbonated water once daily (QD) or twice daily (BID), as assigned/selected by cohort, in continuous 28-day treatment cycles. Dosing is performed in a fasting state: no food or drink other than water for at least 2 hours before and 1 hour after dosing. The starting dose is 150 mg QD. If supported by healthy-volunteer data, 150 mg QD and 75 mg BID cohorts may be enrolled concurrently. Step-up dosing may be used based on emerging safety, pharmacokinetic, and pharmacodynamic data. For protocol-specified patients assigned to 150 mg BID, the step-up schedule may be 25 mg BID on Day 1, 50 mg BID on Day 2, 75 mg BID on Day 3, 100 mg BID on Day 4, 125 mg BID on Day 5, and 150 mg BID from Day 6 onward. Treatment may continue for up to 24 cycles unless discontinued earlier according to protocol criteria.

## NCT07535489
A Phase 2, Multicenter, Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled, Dose-Ranging Study to Evaluate the Efficacy and Safety of IPG11406 Tablets in Adult Patients With Moderately to Severely Active Ulcerative Colitis

Intervention: : IPG11406 — This intervention refers to IPG11406, an investigational oral tablet being evaluated in a Phase 2, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, dose-ranging study in adult patients with moderately to severely active ulcerative colitis (UC).

IPG11406 is administered twice daily (BID) at three dose levels (10 mg, 20 mg, or 40 mg) for 12 weeks. The formulation is intended for oral administration, with matching placebo used as the control. The primary objective is to assess clinical remission based on the modified Mayo Score at Week 12. Secondary and exploratory endpoints include clinical response, endoscopic/histologic improvement, pharmacokinetics, safety, and changes in inflammatory biomarkers.
: Placebo — This intervention refers to matching placebo oral tablets, identical in appearance, shape, size, and color to the IPG11406 investigational product, used as the control in this Phase 2, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study in adult patients with moderately to severely active ulcerative colitis.

The placebo is administered twice daily (BID) for 12 weeks, following the same dosing schedule as the active IPG11406 treatment arms, to maintain the double-blind study design. It contains no active pharmaceutical ingredient (API) and is formulated to be indistinguishable from IPG11406 tablets for participants, investigators, and study staff.

## NCT07576842
C2001P-CS3 CASCADE: A Feasibility Study of HPV Screening and Management Strategies Utilizing Extended Molecular HPV DNA Genotyping and HPV Viral Load in Women Living With HIV

Intervention: : HPV DNA Testing (Abbott Alinity m HPV Assay) — Women will self-collect a vaginal specimen for primary HPV testing to be evaluated on the Abbott Alinity m platform. The Alinity m HR HPV assay is a qualitative, real-time polymerase chain reaction (PCR) assay for the detection of high-risk HPV DNA. The assay detects 14 hrHPV genotypes by targeting the conserved L1 region of HPV DNA and provides individual or group-level genotyping results, including separate readouts for HPV 16, HPV 18, and HPV 45, and grouped detection of other high-risk types. The assay also provides a proxy for HPV viral load as measured by the cycle threshold (CT) value for the type- or group-specific readout.
: Visual Inspection with Acetic Acid — Participants with hrHPV detected will undergo visual inspection with acetic acid (VIA) during a speculum examination. Standard acetic acid (3-5%) is applied to the cervix, and the provider will assess for the presence of cervical lesions, determine suitability for ablative treatment, and characterize the transformation zone (TZ1, TZ2, or TZ3). VIA findings will be used to guide participant management and treatment decisions.
: Cervical Histology (Biopsy Procedures) — Cervical histology specimens will be obtained from participants with hrHPV detected. Biopsies may include lesion-directed cervical punch biopsies, endo- and ectocervical soft-brush biopsies, or endocervical curettage (ECC). At least two biopsies will be obtained even if no lesions are seen. For participants undergoing LEEP/LLETZ, histology will be obtained through the excisional procedure. Cervical histology will be processed locally and interpreted according to the lower anogenital squamous terminology (LAST), including p16 testing where available to confirm morphologic-appearing CIN 2.
: Cervical Treatment (Thermal Ablation or LEEP/LLETZ) — Women with HPV 16 and/or 18 will undergo immediate treatment. Women with non-16/18 hrHPV will undergo immediate treatment if cervical lesions are seen on VIA. Women who are not treated but are subsequently found to have cervical high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesions (hHSIL) on histology will return for cervical treatment. Treatment modality will be determined based on the extent of cervical lesions, with thermal ablation (TA) used for lesions appropriate for ablative therapy and LEEP/LLETZ used for more extensive lesions.
Link: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07576842

## NCT07594197
Evaluation of Sensory and Motor Blockade of Ultrasound-Guided Parasacral Ischial Plane Block in Lower Extremity Surgery

Intervention: : Parasacral Ischial Plan Block — The sacral plexus is located within a fascial plane formed by the pelvic fascia anteriorly, the sacrum medially, the piriformis and gluteus maximus muscles posteriorly, and the ischium laterally. The piriformis muscle has no attachment to the ischium and attaches to the greater trochanter laterally. A fascial plane exists between the piriformis muscle and the ischium; this fascial plane extends to the sacral plexus.

Venkataraju et al. stated that in PIP block demonstrations, the needle should be directed and placed towards the posteromedial surface of the ischium. After bone contact, the medication was injected, and it was observed that the medication spread from under the piriformis muscle towards the sacral plexus.
: Sacral plexus block — This block, defined by the parasacral approach, targets the exit point of the plexus at the level of the foramen ischiadicum majus. Unlike distal sciatic blocks, blocking at this level includes the posterior cutaneous femoral nerve, superior/inferior gluteal nerve, and pudendal nerve, along with the ischial nerve. In current practice, ultrasonography (USG) has become the "gold standard"; visualizing the neural structures deep to the piriformis muscle by placing the probe between the lateral sacrum and the iliac wing increases the success rate while minimizing the risk of complications.
Link: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07594197

## NCT07716072
Sociometric Play-based Remediation of Individual Neurodevelopmental Trajectories (SPRINT)

Intervention: : SPRINT Intervention — The SPRINT intervention is a 12-week, home-based, parent-delivered programme designed to promote responsive caregiving, parental and child executive function, emotion regulation, and child's socio-emotional development. The intervention is delivered via the SPRINT app and comprises six concurrent modules: (A) Awareness, (B) Bond, (C) Cognition, (D) Decode, (E) Emotions, and (F) Fun. On average, participants are expected to engage with programme activities for approximately 25 minutes per day. Automated reminders are provided to support adherence, and participant engagement and responses are monitored throughout the intervention. During the intervention period, home visits will also be conducted to provide study devices, programme orientation, training, and technical support. Brief parent-child play interaction recordings collected during these visits may also be used for analysis and to facilitate module content.
: Waitlist Protocol — Participants will complete brief app-based activities during the 12-week waitlist period using the study devices provided. These activities are designed to maintain participant engagement without providing structured training targeting cognitive or socio-emotional skills, and involve simple visual or sensory interactions (e.g., tapping tasks or basic touch-based activities). The app will also send reminders, and activity completion will be logged.

## NCT07793097
Feasibility of MBSR-VR to Reduce Stress Among Emerging Adults With T1D

Intervention: : Mindfulness-Based Stress Reduction - Virtual Reality — Participants will receive group-delivered MBSR adapted for emerging adults with type 1 diabetes and virtual delivery including virtual reality technology. The intervention consists of instruction and practice in meditation, use of mindfulness techniques, the mind-body connection, and group discussions focused on mindfulness practice. MBSR intervention content includes 1) practicing a variety of mindfulness meditations, including sitting meditation, walking meditation, body scan, and mindful movement/gentle yoga; 2) learning to pay attention to, observe and describe moment-to moment experience in a way that promotes acceptance; 3) understanding stress reactions (stress symptoms, causes, effects) and how to create a mindful response to stressful situations; and 4) facilitators and barriers to applying mindfulness to everyday activities including eating, listening, communicating, walking and other activities.
: Stress tip sheet — Participants will receive an educational stress management tip sheet developed by the American Diabetes Association. The resource provides information about the relationship between stress and diabetes, strategies for recognizing signs of stress, and practical techniques for coping with stress, including relaxation, physical activity, social support, and healthy self-care behaviors.

## NCT07887880
A Novel Multimodal Approach to Promote Motor Recovery and Plasticity After Stroke

Intervention: : tRNS (Transcranial Random Noise Stimulation) — Individuals in this group will receive tRNS at 2 mA intensity between 101-640 Hz. The current will be gradually ramped up for and down for the first and last 30 seconds of the stimulation.
: FES (Functional Electrical Stimulation)-assisted task-specific practice — The FES-assisted task-specific practice will focus on restituting the movement components composing functional tasks. We will use the principles of motor learning with FES-assisted task-specific practice. Based on motor learning principles, our intervention will include 1) movement practice as close to normative as possible, 2) a high number of repetitions, 3) attention to the motor task, and 4) training specificity.
: Sham-tRNS (Transcranial Random Noise Stimulation) — Individuals in this group will receive sham-tRNS via the same electrode configuration as the tRNS. The stimulation will gradually ramp up for 30 seconds and then fade away for the rest of the intervention session.

## NCT07891585
Clinical Response, Traditional Chinese Medicine Syndrome Patterns, and Brain Functional Characteristics Associated With Laser Acupuncture in Chronic Migraine

Intervention: : 810 nm laser acupuncture — Participants will receive noninvasive laser acupuncture using an 810-nm near-infrared laser with an output power of 150 mW. Laser irradiation will be applied to 13 standardized acupoints: bilateral Fengchi (GB20), Shuaigu (GB8), Taiyang (EX-HN5), Zanzhu (BL2), Hegu (LI4), Taichong (LR3), and unilateral Yintang (EX-HN3). Each acupoint will be irradiated for 30 seconds, delivering 4.5 J of energy per point. Treatment will be administered twice weekly for four consecutive weeks, for a total of eight sessions. The same standardized treatment protocol will be used for participants with chronic migraine assigned to the active laser acupuncture group and healthy volunteers receiving active laser acupuncture.
: Sham Laser Acupuncture — Participants assigned to the sham laser acupuncture group will undergo a procedure identical to active laser acupuncture, using the same laser device, standardized acupoints, treatment duration, and operating procedures, but without emission of therapeutic laser energy. The sham procedure will target the same 13 acupoints: bilateral Fengchi (GB20), Shuaigu (GB8), Taiyang (EX-HN5), Zanzhu (BL2), Hegu (LI4), Taichong (LR3), and unilateral Yintang (EX-HN3). Each acupoint will be treated for 30 seconds. Sham treatment will be administered twice weekly for four consecutive weeks, for a total of eight sessions. The procedure is designed to maintain participant blinding and serve as a placebo control for active laser acupuncture.
Link: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07891585

SUMMARY:

## NCT07892742
The Effects of Increased Water Intake on Muscle Function, Physical Performance, and Endocrine Regulation in Low-Drinking Older Adults: A Randomized Controlled Trial

Intervention: : Water — Participants will be assigned at random to either the experimental group (EG) or the control group (CG). Over the 7-day intervention period, the EG will be asked to increase total daily water intake (WI) to at least 45 mL·kg-¹·day-¹, while the CG will continue their usual water consumption, corresponding to ≤35 mL·kg-¹·day-¹. Total WI will account for water obtained from both beverages and food.

Participants allocated to the EG will be instructed to keep their usual dietary habits unchanged during the intervention so that the amount of water derived from food remains comparable to habitual intake. Accordingly, the intervention will involve an increase in fluid consumption only. The additional amount of water required to reach the target of ≥45 mL·kg-¹·day-¹ will be individually determined based on body mass and the estimated contribution of food to total WI. Vimeiro Original natural mineral water will be used as the additional source of fluid.
Link: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07892742

## NCT07931131
One Session Treatment for Dental Phobia in an Underserved Population

Intervention: : One-Session Treatment for Dental Phobia (OSTD) — OSTD is a single-session behavioral intervention designed to reduce dental phobia in children and adolescents. The intervention uses individualized, graduated exposure to feared dental situations and procedures. Exposure activities are guided by a participant-specific fear hierarchy and cognitive-behavioral assessment developed before treatment. During the treatment session, participants engage in exposure exercises intended to help them confront feared dental situations and develop new learning about anticipated negative outcomes.
: Psychoeducation and Relaxation Training (RELAX) — RELAX is a single-session behavioral comparison intervention consisting of psychoeducation and relaxation training for children and adolescents with dental phobia. The intervention includes information about dental-related fear and anxiety and instruction in relaxation strategies, including progressive muscle relaxation. Participants receive guided relaxation training intended to support the management of anxiety associated with dental situations.

## NCT07931300
Multicenter Real-world Study of SIS Reinforcement Patch in High-risk Colorectal Anastomosis and Exploration of the Mechanism Promoting Anastomotic Healing

Intervention: : SIS Patch Intervention for High - Risk Colorectal Anastomosis — This intervention uses a Small Intestinal Submucosa (SIS) patch (a medical device) to reinforce anastomosis during gastrointestinal anastomosis surgery, targeting patients with high-risk factors for colorectal anastomotic leakage.

Preoperatively, subjects are screened for high-risk factors (e.g., abdominopelvic abscess from gastrointestinal perforation, ulcerative colitis history, hormone therapy within 6 months, etc.). On Study Day 0 (surgery day), the SIS patch is applied during colorectal anastomosis, with intraoperative observation of immediate stapling effect (e.g., seromuscular dehiscence, bleeding).

Postoperatively, subjects are followed up at 1, 3, 6 months to monitor anastomotic leakage, healing and adverse events. It differs from conventional anastomosis by focusing on high-risk populations, with intraoperative and long-term assessments to prevent anastomotic leakage.
Link: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07931300

## NCT07932652
Increasing Human Milk Feeding in the Neonatal ICU

Intervention: : Motivational Interviewing (MI) and Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT) (MIACT) — MIACT interventions will occur within conventional lactation visits, during which specialists often guide, observe, and troubleshoot with mothers. The lactation service consults mothers in \<24 hours, again \<48 hours, and at 1-week and 2-weeks post-delivery, and additional lactation consults at common periods of MOM decline (e.g., 1 month) will be offered.

Sessions span 10-60 minutes and lactation specialists will use MIACT strategies, based on each mothers' needs to: (1) assess current MOM-feeding motivation (via R-I-C rulers \[see Table 1\]), (2) discuss challenges; (3) identify obstacles (e.g., lack of perceived control); (4) foster learning/practice of acceptance and willingness (i.e., alternative skills); and, (5) encourage value-based goals (i.e., initiate/sustain MOM feeding). Follow-up consults will revisit content and obstacles, review progress, re-assess motivation, practice alternative skills, identify new strategies, and affirm value-based action.
: Usual Lactation Support — Conventional lactation visits, during which specialists often guide, observe, and troubleshoot with mothers. The lactation service consults mothers in \<24 hours, again \<48 hours, and at 1-week and 2-weeks post-delivery.

## NCT07932665
TELE-ASD-PEDS-Preschool (TAP-P) Psychometrics and Decision Support for Preschool Autism Tele-Assessment

Intervention: : Tele-assessment using the TAP-P — The TAP-P was developed specifically for telemedicine-based autism assessment of preschool-aged children. It has distinct administration and scoring procedures for children with less verbal language (TAP-P Form 1) and those with more verbal language (TAP-P Form 2). All children first complete an initial set of clinician-guided, caregiver-mediated activities, including independent play, interactive play with caregiver, turn-taking, and bids for social responding. TAP-P Form 1 procedures include activities that elicit a child's social play, requesting strategies, and response to caregiver interference in play. TAP-P Form 2 procedures include additional caregiver-mediated activities (i.e., caregiver-led play) and clinician-mediated activities (i.e., drawing and show-and-tell activities; prompts for conversation). Following TAP-P administration, clinicians score observed child behaviors associated with possible autism.
Link: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07932665
