## NCT07932691
A Multicenter, Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled Phase I Study to Evaluate the Safety, Tolerability, Pharmacokinetics, and Pharmacodynamics of Single and Multiple Ascending Doses of VDJ010 for Subcutaneous Injection in Healthy Chinese Subjects and Patients With Ulcerative Colitis

Intervention: : Recombinant Human Interleukin-2 Fusion Protein with Human Serum Albumin (VDJ010) — VDJ010 is a recombinant fusion protein consisting of human interleukin-2 (IL-2) genetically fused to human serum albumin (HSA), produced using Chinese hamster ovary (CHO) cells through DNA recombinant technology. The fusion protein selectively binds to the high-affinity IL-2 receptor (IL-2Rαβγ) constitutively expressed on regulatory T cells (Treg), thereby promoting Treg expansion and restoring immune tolerance in autoimmune diseases such as ulcerative colitis. The HSA moiety extends the plasma half-life of IL-2 to enable less frequent subcutaneous dosing.
: Placebo — This is a matching placebo formulation containing no active pharmaceutical ingredient (API). The placebo is manufactured to be identical in appearance, color, shape, size, and packaging to the investigational product VDJ010 to maintain the integrity of the double-blind design. It is utilized solely as a control intervention for the purpose of this randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase I clinical trial.

## NCT06817564
Effects of an AI-driven Personalized Exercise Feedback Program on Exercise Adherence and Health Outcomes in Patients With Traumatic Brain Injury

Intervention: : AI-PEF — Participants will follow a 24-week walking program with at least three 30-minute sessions per week, with exercise intensity progressively adjusted based on heart rate and effort indices. Garmin fitness trackers will monitor exercise adherence and intensity. Remote guidance will be provided through five AI-generated digital health messages per week via LINE, delivered on Monday, Tuesday, Thursday, Friday, and Saturday, and tailored to participants' exercise performance and individualized goals established during the remote exercise intervention and consultation. The messages will include exercise performance feedback, goal setting and reinforcement, exercise and device-use reminders, health education, and encouragement and support. The digital component will allow participants to share their progress and seek guidance during scheduled in-person consultations. AI-driven digital feedback provides a convenient and accessible approach to supporting participants in engaging in exercise.
: Theory-based digital exercise — The theory-based digital exercise group will follow the same in-person clinic visits, assessment schedule, and 24-week walking program as the AI-PEF group. Garmin fitness trackers will be used to monitor exercise adherence and intensity. The research team will deliver five standardized digital health messages per week during the initial 12 weeks through the LINE app using message templates developed in advance. The messages will include exercise guidance, goal setting and reinforcement, exercise and device-use reminders, health education and lifestyle recommendations, and encouragement and support. The messages will not be generated or tailored by AI, and participants will not receive AI-driven personalized feedback.
: Active Control — Participants in the active control group will receive standard TBI care, including routine clinic visits. In addition, Garmin fitness trackers will be provided for self-monitoring during the study. The research team will deliver five standardized general health messages per week during the initial 12 weeks through the LINE app. The messages will include TBI-related health education, general health and lifestyle information, general recommendations for daily physical activity, general check-in messages, and technical reminders for Garmin use. The messages will not include structured exercise guidance, individualized goal setting or reinforcement, performance-based feedback, or AI-generated personalized feedback. Participants completing the 6-month protocol will have the option to access the AI-PEF program after the study.
Link: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT06817564

## NCT07767123
Development and Validation of an Artificial Intelligence-Based Rehabilitation Program for Dysphagia

Intervention: : Neuromuscular electrical stimulation for swallowing — Participants receive neuromuscular electrical stimulation (NMES) applied to swallowing-related muscles as part of swallowing rehabilitation. The stimulation parameters are individualized using an AI-assisted optimization process. The AI model analyzes swallowing assessment data, including FEES findings and multi-sensor signals, to select parameters expected to improve swallowing. The selected parameters are then applied. This intervention differs from conventional methods because the stimulation parameters are not selected solely by clinician experience, but are optimized by an AI-assisted system based on the participant's swallowing assessment results.
: Multi-sensor swallowing screening for dysphagia — Participants undergo a multi-sensor screening test for dysphagia. During swallowing, signals are collected from multiple sensors, such as surface electromyography, acoustic sensors, oxygen saturation, and respiratory sensors. The signals are analyzed using AI-assisted algorithms to identify patterns associated with swallowing impairment and aspiration risk. This approach provides objective, quantitative swallowing assessment and may be compared with FEES. It differs from conventional bedside screening and FEES by combining multiple physiological signals.
Link: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07767123

Implementing Brain Health PRO - A Dementia Risk Reduction Program - Across Diverse Settings, With Emphasis on Rural and Underserved Communities: Phase 2

Intervention: : Brain Health PRO (BHPRO) — A 6-month, web-based dementia-risk-reduction program consisting of eight modules addressing modifiable risk factors: physical activity, diet, cognitive engagement, sleep, social and psychological health, vascular health, and vision/hearing health. Upon registration, participants complete baseline lifestyle questionnaires that generate a personalized risk profile. Participants are instructed to prioritize three risk domains based on their profile and receive tailored content accordingly. ## NCT07935681
The Effect of Foley Catheter Versus Foley Plus Extra-amniotic Saline Infusion on Bishop Progression, Labor Parameters, and Perinatal Outcomes in Pregnancies at 41 Weeks and Beyond: A Randomized Controlled Trial"

Intervention: : Foley Catheter with Extra-amniotic Saline Infusion (EASI) — A single-balloon Foley catheter (16-18 French) is inserted through the internal os of the cervix into the extra-amniotic space under aseptic conditions. The balloon is inflated with 30-50 ml of sterile saline. Following placement, a continuous extra-amniotic saline infusion (EASI) is administered through the catheter at a constant rate of 30 ml per hour using an infusion pump. The procedure aims to induce cervical ripening through both mechanical pressure and biochemical stimulation.
: Foley Catheter Alone — A single-balloon Foley catheter (16-18 French) is inserted through the internal os of the cervix into the extra-amniotic space under aseptic conditions. The balloon is inflated with 30-50 ml of sterile saline. The catheter is then taped to the inner thigh of the patient to maintain tension. No saline infusion is administered in this group. The catheter remains in place until spontaneous expulsion or for a maximum duration of 12 hours.

## NCT07935980
Intradialytic Benson's Relaxation Technique on Dialysis Adequacy and Sleep Quality in Patients With Chronic Kidney Disease

Intervention: : Benson's relaxation technique — Research has shown that the Benson Relaxation Technique (BRT) is an effective strategy for decreasing sleep disruptions in older persons and hemodialysis patients with hypertension focuses on deep rhythmic breathing and mental focusing rather than physical muscle tensing. Steps :

1\. Find a quiet environment: Sit or lie down in a comfortable, quiet space where you will not be disturbed. 2. Close your eyes: Gently close your eyes to block out visual distractions.3. Relax your muscles: Release all tension from your body, moving progressively from your feet up to your face (or top of your head).4. Breathe through your nose: Become aware of your natural breathing. As you exhale, silently repeat a chosen focus word or phrase-such as "one", "calm", or "peace"-to yourself (e.g., inhale... exhale, "one").5. Maintain a passive attitude: When distracting thoughts drift into your mind, do not fight them or judge yourself.6.Practice for 10 to 20 minutes7.Transition slowly
: Control group — Aerobic ex by using mini pedal exerciser without involving benson's relaxation technique.

for 12 weeks , 30 minutes in the first 2 hours of dialysis session

## NCT07936266
A Phase I Open-label, Multicenter Trial of Asciminib (ABL001) Added to Inotuzumab Ozogamicin (Besponsa®) in Patients With Relapsed or Refractory Philadelphia Chromosome-positive B-cell Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia

Intervention: : Asciminib — Asciminib is a first-in-class STAMP (Specifically Targeting the ABL Myristoyl Pocket), and is an approved TKI in newly-diagnosed and previously-treated chronic myeloid leukemia (CML). It is a non-chemotherapeutic, oral agent which specifically and potently targets the mutant Philadelphia chromosome driven by t(9;22). Due to its novel mechanism of action as a STAMP, asciminib is active in the setting of mutations in the BCR-ABL ATP-binding pocket including the T315I gatekeeper mutations, which confers resistance to first- and second-generation tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs). Asciminib has not yet been studied in Philadelphia-chromosome positive B-ALL.
: Inotuzumab ozogamicin — Inotuzumab ozogamicin (INO) is an antibody-drug conjugate which targets CD22, an antigen present in \>90% of B-ALL cases. INO is FDA approved and a standard-of-care treatment in relapsed/refractory B-ALL. The drug is approved and active in Ph-positive and -negative disease.
Link: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07936266

## NCT07936461
Pilot Feasibility Study of an Occupation-Based Immersive Virtual Reality Intervention for Upper-Limb Rehabilitation After Stroke

Intervention: : Occupation-Based Immersive Virtual Reality Rehabilitation — The intervention consists of 12 supervised immersive virtual reality (IVR) sessions using two occupation-based applications: Virtual Gardening and Virtual Painting. Each session is planned to include approximately 30 minutes of virtual activities: 10 minutes of structured Gardening, 10 minutes of structured Painting, 5 minutes of free Gardening, and 5 minutes of free Painting.

Gardening activities include reaching toward leaves, harvesting virtual olives, planting seeds, and watering plants. Painting activities include tracing geometric and representational shapes and creating drawings using virtual brushes and colours.

The applications provide graded task difficulty, affected-hand interaction, mirrored control using the unaffected hand, and free exploration. Participants interact with the virtual environment using a Meta Quest 2 head-mounted display and controllers while seated, under therapist supervision. Rest breaks and assistance are provided according to individual needs.
Link: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07936461

## NCT06262334
Developing a Community-Informed, Peer-to-Peer Intervention to Improve Health-Related Quality of Life Among African American Men

Intervention: : The Fade to Fitness Program — The Fade to Fitness Program is a group-based and barbershop-based behavioral intervention to improve health-related quality of life among African American men. The program is unique because it is culturally targeted and individually tailored. The culturally targeted content was developed following barbershop-based focus groups. The Fade to Fitness Program targets four behaviors strongly linked to health-related quality of life among African American men - physical activity, healthy eating, stress management, and depression management. During the group-based portion of the program, Motivational Interviewing is used by the facilitator as a conversational approach to enhance participants\&#39; motivation and commitment towards positive behavior change. The goal is to foster intrinsic motivation among participants to engage in these behaviors. It is individually tailored by encouraging participants to identify personal values and linking them to health promoting behaviors.
Link: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT06262334

## NCT06509152
Theory of Mind-based Social Competence Group Intervention (ToM-SCGI) in Children With Autism Spectrum Disorder: a Randomized Controlled Trial

Intervention: : Theory of mind-based social competence group intervention — The ToM-SCGI is designed as a group intervention, with 60-minute sessions held weekly, either once or twice, and led by trained therapists. Two caregiver meetings are conducted in the middle and end of the interventions.

The intervention process for each session is as follows:

1. Warm-up Activities(5-10 minutes): review the previous group session and prepare for the current group activities.
2. Theory of Mind Instruction(10-15 minutes): based on the developmental stage of the children's theory of mind, using thought bubbles to teach corresponding elements of theory of mind development.
3. Social Skills Group Games(30-35 minutes): design social scenario-based group games that allow children to practice applying the acquired theory of mind abilities into expressions and applications of theory of mind and social competence.
4. Summary(5-10 minutes): summarize the children's performance in the group and assign homework.
Link: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT06509152

## NCT07464002
Studie Zum Habituellen Durst Und Adapt Durst Studie: Habitual Thirst Study and Adapt Thirst Study

Intervention: : Drinking water to dilute urine — After Weeks 1-4 baseline data collection, people randomized in Week 5 will be instructed to increase drinking water to approx. 4 times 500 mL/d in Weeks 6-9 to reach a volume that is enough to dilute urine specific gravity below 1.013 everyday. The plain water intake (PWI) exposure is approx. 20 mL/kg PWI for men, 25 mL/kg PWI for women. Addition of PWI to the diet may increase total water intake (TWI) and minimally displace some other beverage intake. Based on Adapt Study data, the hypo-osmotic share of TWI is expected to increase from below 50% to 50% or higher. The intervention dose is also aligned with observational data from the Paracelsus 10000 study in Salzburg, which found that healthy adults who met hydration criteria reported at least 1L/d PWI. The intervention will be communicated to participants in terms of L/d instead of mL/kg, because L/d are easier to translate into portion size and drinking behavior.
Link: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07464002

## NCT07554690
Photobiomodulation Laser in Reticular Pseudodrusen Secondary to Age-related Macular Degeneration

Intervention: : Photobiomodulation Therapy — Photobiomodulation (PBM) therapy is delivered using a CE-marked medical device (EYE-LIGHT®, Espansione Group S.p.A., Italy). The treatment consists of two cycles: the first cycle includes 8 sessions over 4 weeks (two sessions per week), and the second cycle includes 6 sessions over 3 weeks. Each session lasts approximately 12 minutes and is performed under standardized conditions.

The device delivers low-energy light at specific wavelengths (approximately 590 nm and 630 nm) in both continuous and pulsed modes. The treatment is non-invasive and does not produce thermal damage, aiming to stimulate mitochondrial activity, reduce oxidative stress, and modulate inflammatory pathways in retinal cells.
: Sham Photobiomodulation — The sham intervention is delivered using the same device and procedures as the active photobiomodulation treatment, including identical session number, duration, and schedule, to maintain masking conditions.

However, the device delivers minimal, non-therapeutic light energy (approximately 2.5 mW/cm² ±20% and 5.5 mW/cm² ±20%), which is insufficient to produce a biological effect. This approach ensures that participants experience similar treatment conditions without receiving active photobiomodulation therapy.
Link: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07554690

## NCT07589062
HEAL MS: A Culturally Adapted Lifestyle Medicine Intervention Targeting Metabolic and Immune Dysregulation in Multiple Sclerosis Using Multi-Omics Profiling

Intervention: : Multi-Domain Lifestyle Intervention — The intervention is a 12-week multi-domain lifestyle program. It targets four behavioral domains: physical activity, nutrition, sleep, and stress regulation. Participants attend twice-weekly supervised online exercise sessions using scalable functional movements performed with bodyweight, resistance bands, and suspension training. The nutrition component provides individualized meal plans based on maintenance calories, emphasizing anti-inflammatory, whole-food nutrition with a macronutrient distribution of approximately 40% carbohydrates, 30% protein, and 30% fat. During the first two weeks, meals are delivered to support adherence. Sleep optimization focuses on circadian-aligned behaviors such as consistent sleep timing and reduced evening light exposure. Stress regulation includes daily breathing exercises, mindfulness practices, and vagal nerve-stimulating techniques. Participants track dadaily behaviors, wellbeing, and wearable data using a billiungual mobile app.

## NCT07797530
The Effectiveness of Breathing Training in Subacute Neck Pain

Intervention: : Active Cycle of Breathing Technique — The patient will sit comfortably in a chair in a quiet environment, with shoulders relaxed, and will be instructed to perform deep, slow breathing with prolonged exhalation. The cycle will be: Breathing Control-Thoracic Expansion Exercise (TEE)-Breathing Control-Thoracic Expansion Exercise-Breathing Control-Bilateral Thoracic Expansion Exercise (BTEE)-Breathing Control. Each step will be repeated 3-5 times. During TEE and BTEE, proprioceptive tactile stimulation will be applied by resistance during inhalation. The application procedure will be taught in sessions 1 and 2. At home, the patient will place their own hand where the therapist normally places theirs. The program will be performed 3 days/week for 6 weeks, 15-20 minutes/session. Participants will also be instructed to perform the technique at home twice daily.
: Active Comparator: Progressive Muscle Relaxation — The patient will wear comfortable clothing and sit in a quiet environment. During Progressive Muscle Relaxation, the eyes will be closed and attention will be focused on the body, particularly on muscle tension and relaxation. The session will begin with deep breathing and relaxing music. During inhalation, each muscle group will be contracted for 5 seconds and relaxed for 10 seconds during exhalation, while other muscles remain relaxed. The technique will be applied in order to the hands, arms, face, neck, shoulders, chest, abdomen, back, hips, thighs, lower legs, and feet. At the end, all muscles will be contracted and relaxed together, and the relaxed position will be maintained for 2 minutes. The program will be performed 3 days/week for 6 weeks, 15-20 minutes/session.Participants will also be instructed to perform the technique at home twice daily.
: Exercise Program — The exercise program will include active range of motion (AROM), stretching, scapular stabilization, deep cervical muscle, and postural exercises.

During weeks 1-2, the exercises will be performed as 1 set, progressing to 2 sets in week 3.

From week 4, resistance will be added to selected exercises as appropriate. These exercises will be performed as 1 set during weeks 4-5 and 2 sets during week 6.

The program will be performed under the supervision of a physiotherapist 3 days per week for 6 weeks, for a total of 18 sessions, with each session lasting 15-20 minutes. Participants will also be instructed to perform the exercises at home twice daily.
: Traditional Physiotherapy — Traditional physiotherapy will consist of electrotherapy modalities, including hot pack, ultrasound, interferential current, and transcutaneous electrical nerve stimulation (TENS). Traditional physiotherapy will be provided 5 days per week for 3 weeks, with each treatment session lasting 45 minutes.
Link: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07797530

## NCT07865858
Development and Evaluation of an Indigenized Family Acceptance Project for Lakota 2SLGBTQ+ Teens (PHASE III: PILOT RANDOMIZED CONTROLLED TRIAL )

Intervention: : Adapted Lakota Family Acceptance Program — Tiwahe Tewichaglapi ("The Family Loves Them") Program Overview Tiwahe Tewichaglapi is a culturally grounded, family-centered intervention adapted from the Family Acceptance Project® (FAP) to promote caregiver acceptance, respect, support, and family bonding for 2SLGBTQ+ Lakota youth. The program was developed in partnership with the Lakota Oyate to address family rejection rooted in colonization and historical trauma and to honor traditional Two Spirit roles that have long held important and respected places within Lakota communities. The program aims to strengthen families, increase youth pride and hope for the future, and reduce mental health risks such as depression, anxiety, substance use, dating violence, and suicide among 2SLGBTQ+ Lakota youth. The program includes eight family group sessions 2.5 hrs. each delivered by Lakota facilitators that include Lakota cultural and spiritual practices - including smudging, a Lakota prayer, and a shared meal.

## NCT07910864
Effect of Preoperative Ultrasound-Guided Bilateral Greater Occipital Nerve Block on Postoperative Headache Following Endovascular Coiling of Unruptured Intracranial Aneurysms: A Prospective, Randomized, Sham-Controlled Trial

Intervention: : Ultrasound-Guided Bilateral Greater Occipital Nerve Block — Ultrasound-guided bilateral greater occipital nerve block will be performed before general anesthesia induction using a high-frequency linear ultrasound transducer.

The greater occipital nerve will be identified between the semispinalis capitis and obliquus capitis inferior muscles. A 25-gauge, 50-mm echogenic needle will be advanced under continuous ultrasound guidance using an in-plane approach.

Following color Doppler assessment and negative aspiration, 3 mL of 0.25% bupivacaine (7.5 mg) will be injected slowly and incrementally on each side.

The total bilateral dose will be 15 mg of bupivacaine.
: Bilateral Superficial Subcutaneous Sham Injection — A bilateral superficial subcutaneous sham injection will be performed before general anesthesia induction.

Following standardized positioning, skin antisepsis, and ultrasound examination, a short 27-gauge needle will be used to administer 0.5 mL of 0.9% normal saline subcutaneously on each side of the occipital region.

The total bilateral injection volume will be 1 mL.

The needle will not be advanced into the deep interfascial plane, and the greater occipital nerve will not be directly targeted.
Link: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07910864

SUMMARY:

## NCT07929688
La Restriction de l'Usage Des réseaux Sociaux et Ses Effets Sur l'anxiété Sociale, la Peur de Passer à côté et la qualité de Vie liée à la santé : un Essai contrôlé randomisé

Intervention: : Social media restriction — Participants in the intervention group will be instructed to restrict their total daily use of the social media platforms to one hour for one week. This limit applies to the total time spent on all included platforms, not to each platform separately. This limit of one hour per day is based on Davis and Goldfield's (2025) RCT, in which restricting use of seven social media platforms to one hour per day for three weeks was found to significantly reduce symptoms of anxiety, depression, and FoMO. We expect that our short intervention would be more feasible and acceptable for students, thus improving adherence. It will provide additional evidence of the potential benefits of short-term interventions.

## NCT07932509
Effect of Targeted Tracheal Kinesio Taping on Cough Efficacy and Decannulation Time in Burned Patients

Intervention: : Tracheal Kinesio Taping — * Tracheal and Glottic Stabilization (Strip 1): An "I-strip" will be tailored to bridge horizontally across the anterior neck. The center of the tape will be applied directly superior to the tracheostoma flap (overlying the thyroid and cricoid cartilages) utilizing a facilitation tension of 25-35% stretch. This anchors structural airway positioning during explosive exhalation. The final 3 cm of each tail will be laid down laterally over the sternocleidomastoid muscles with 0% tension to act as neutral anchors.
* Accessory Expiratory Muscle Assist (Strip 2): A "Y-strip" will be measured from the sternal notch to the clavicular heads. The base of the Y-strip will be anchored at the manubrium of the sternum with no tension. The two tails will then be directed superiorly and laterally along the trajectories of the infrahyoid and sternocleidomastoid muscles, applied with a light recoil tension of 15-20% stretch to biomechanically assist accessory expiratory acceleration during a cough.
: Control — standardized daily chest physiotherapy protocol tailored for burn critical care. This encompasses early progressive mobility and ambulation, targeted diaphragmatic breathing exercises, active-assisted or manually assisted coughing, oropharyngeal secretion suctioning
Link: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07932509

## NCT07937345
Effect of Eccentric Versus Concentric Ankle Dorsiflexor Training on Dynamic Plantar Pressure Parameters During Walking in Patients With Multiple Sclerosis

Intervention: : Eccentric Ankle Dorsiflexor Elastic-Band Training — Participants will begin with the ankle positioned in dorsiflexion. A graded elastic resistance band attached to the forefoot will apply a plantarflexion-directed force. Participants will slowly control movement toward plantarflexion against band resistance, producing eccentric contraction of the ankle dorsiflexor muscles. Return to the starting position will be passive or assisted to minimize concentric dorsiflexor activity. Training will consist of three sets of ten repetitions per session, with one to two minutes of rest between sets. Sessions will occur three times weekly for six weeks. Band resistance will progress weekly according to participant tolerance and movement quality.
: Concentric Ankle Dorsiflexor Elastic-Band Training — Participants will begin with the ankle positioned in plantarflexion. A graded elastic resistance band attached to the forefoot will oppose active dorsiflexion. Participants will actively move the ankle from plantarflexion toward dorsiflexion against resistance, producing concentric contraction of the ankle dorsiflexor muscles. Return toward plantarflexion will be assisted or performed with minimal resistance to minimize the eccentric training component. Training will consist of three sets of ten repetitions per session, with one to two minutes of rest between sets. Sessions will occur three times weekly for six weeks, with weekly progression based on tolerance and movement control.
: standardized Conventional Physical Therapy for Multiple Sclerosis — Both groups will receive identical conventional physical therapy consisting of upper-limb strengthening for shoulder and elbow muscle groups; flexibility exercises with 20-60-second stretching holds; postural correction; abdominal and trunk-extensor strengthening; relaxation and controlled breathing; and education on fatigue management and energy conservation. Upper-limb and trunk exercises will generally involve 5-10 repetitions with progression according to tolerance. Conventional therapy and ankle-specific resistance exercises will be delivered within 45-minute treatment sessions, three times weekly for six weeks.
Link: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07937345

## NCT07938593
Preventing Mood Disorders in High-risk Offspring: Protocol for the Randomized Controlled Trial of the MARIO Online Preventive Intervention Platform

Intervention: : KOPPsupport — KOPPsupport is an existing psycho-educational program for COPMI, developed by the Trimbos institute for participants aged 16 to 25 years (Woolderink et al., 2010). It is designed to strengthen protective factors to prevent mental health issues. Registration occurs via the MARIO platform, after which participants are redirected to the KOPPsupport website (https://www.koppsupport.nl/) where they can sign up for a specific starting date. Depending on group start dates, participants may wait for up to 4 weeks before starting the intervention. The intervention itself consists of eight weekly online chat group meetings, guided by mental health professionals. The sessions cover topics including thoughts and feelings, questions about addictions and mental problems, roles in the family, and different styles of behavior. Before each session, participants are also required to carry out homework assignments about the topic that will subsequently be discussed in that session.
: Moodpep — Moodpep is an online preventive intervention with CBT-based elements (VUmc; Garnefski \& Kraaij, 2023). While Moodpep is developed for individuals aged 18 years and older, participants younger than 18 can still select it on the MARIO intervention platform. It consists of 7 different modules in a fixed order that participants are instructed to complete within 8 weeks. The CBT-based modules aim to encourage new activities, improve relaxation, reduce negative thoughts, and assist in working towards personal goals. Tasks within the modules include the completion of a daily diary, different psychoeducational exercises, and suggestions for COPMI to develop ideas about reaching personal goals. Users are also in regular online contact with a trained coach who is a member of the MARIO research team. The coach gives asynchronous feedback within 3 working days about the participants' completed modules, is available to talk about potential problems, and encourages continued participation.
: Grow It! — Grow It! is a gamified smartphone app for youth between the ages of 10 and 25 years. The app consists of three major components: 1) Increasing affective awareness via ESM surveys; 2) improving emotional reflection via a personalized visual mood profile; and 3) improving adaptive coping through daily CBT-based challenges.

To improve app interactivity, fun, and user friendliness, the app includes the choice for an avatar and other ways to personalize the app. Participants use the Grow It! app for four weeks. There must be at least 4 people available to build a team for the intervention to start. If less than 4 people sign up over the course of these four weeks, the remaining spots are filled by members of the research team who are instructed to also use Grow It! regularly during the intervention period.
Link: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07938593

SUMMARY:

A neutral self-adhesive electrode is placed on the lower abdomen; the optimal stimulation point at the lateral edge of the popliteal fossa is identified by a rhythmic motor response of the leg, and the stimulation voltage is set to the lowest value that evokes this response. Stimulation lasts 30 minutes, once a week for 12 weeks (12 sessions). The device emits a 4 Hz acoustic signal.
: Sham peroneal transcutaneous neuromodulation (URIS I, Stimvia) — Identical preparation, electrode placement and duration as active stimulation, but the stimulation voltage is set to 0 V bilaterally so that no stimulation is delivered. Exposure to active stimulation is limited to the minimum needed to locate the stimulation point. 30 minutes, once a week for 12 weeks (12 sessions). The device emits the same 4 Hz acoustic signal.

## NCT06971705
A Study on Precise Cerebral Localization and Network Mechanisms of Repetitive Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation in Treating Chronic Ankle Instability Based on High-resolution Functional Magnetic Resonance Imaging

Intervention: : repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation, rTMS — Participants underwent rTMS intervention prior to daily ankle stability training. The interventional targets were the key cortical brain regions identified in preliminary studies, with stimulation applied to the contralateral cortical areas corresponding to the affected ankle joint. Parameters included a double-cone coil, 10 Hz frequency, 2-second stimulation duration, 8-second inter-train intervals, 60 repetitions, totaling 1,200 pulses per session, with each session lasting 10 minutes. Ankle stability training commenced within 10 minutes post-rTMS, following the same duration and intensity as the Ankle Stability Training Group + Sham rTMS Group. The treatment was conducted three times per week for a total of 4 weeks.
: ankle stability training — The ankle stability training protocol comprised three modalities: neuromuscular training, balance training, and proprioceptive training. Specific exercises included single-leg stance, balance pad training, heel raises, resistive ankle inversion/eversion exercises, MOBO board balance exercises, alphabet tracing (toe-writing), lateral walking, heel walking, toe walking, and jump and landing control drills. The training progressed from stable to unstable surfaces, starting at low intensity and gradually increasing in difficulty and intensity. The training was conducted three times per week for a total of 4 weeks.
: Sham repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation, SrTMS — Before each session of ankle stability training, participants received sham rTMS intervention. The sham stimulation mimicked the sensory experience of real rTMS but did not produce any physiological effects.
Link: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT06971705

## NCT07242690
Advancing PET-CT Imaging With Photon Counting Detector CT

Intervention: : PCD-CT — A direct qualitative comparison of the subjective PET image quality will be performed.

Two blinded board-certified radiologists/nuclear medicine physicians will independently review PET images constructed using non-contrast PCD-CT data as well as PET images constructed using standard of care non-contrast EID-CT data in random order. Both raters will assess PET images subjectively regarding overall image quality using a five-point Likert scale. The rating will be defined as: (1) non-diagnostic - insufficient diagnostic confidence, (2) poor - low diagnostic confidence, (3) moderate - average diagnostic confidence; (4) good - high diagnostic confidence, and (5) excellent - full diagnostic confidence.
: PET CT — To compare the subjective image quality of PET images constructed using non-contrast PCD-CT image data to PET images constructed using conventional standard-of-care non-contrast EID-CT image data by performing a qualitative analysis of diagnostic confidence as determined by board-certified radiologists/nuclear medicine physicians during image review.

## NCT07722559
The Short-Term Impact of Manual Traction Combined With Standard Rehabilitation Protocol on Pain, Function, and Quality of Life After Total Knee Arthroplasty

Intervention: : Manual Tibiofemoral Traction — Participants will receive manual tibiofemoral traction combined with a standardized rehabilitation program following total knee arthroplasty. During the first postoperative week, all participants will receive standard rehabilitation without traction. Manual traction will begin in the second postoperative week and will be applied by a physiotherapist using the Kaltenborn technique. The distal femur will be stabilized with a fixation belt, while a separate traction belt around the distal tibia and fibula will apply tibiofemoral traction with the knee in extension. Traction will progress over three weeks: Grade I in week 2 (10-15% body weight), Grade II in week 3 (15-20%), and Grade III in week 4 (20-25%). The traction grade and force will be adjusted according to patient tolerance and postoperative safety. Each session will include 30-60 seconds of traction followed by a 15-second rest interval, repeated for eight cycles. After each session, ROM (20 active,20 assisted) will be performed.
: Sham Tibiofemoral Traction — Participants assigned to the control group will receive sham tibiofemoral traction combined with the standardized rehabilitation program following total knee arthroplasty. Sham traction will simulate the manual traction procedure without the application of therapeutic traction force. The procedure will be performed to maintain participant blinding while providing the same rehabilitation protocol as the intervention group.
Link: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07722559

SUMMARY:

## NCT07811921
Evaluation of the Effects of Peri-implantitis Treatment Approaches on Titanium Particle Release

Intervention: : Mechanical Debridement with Titanium Curettes — This arm evaluates standard mechanical debridement using medical-grade titanium curettes, applied as 10-15 systematic strokes per implant surface horizontally and apico-coronally. Unlike conventional studies that focus solely on clinical indices, this protocol uniquely combines mechanical cleaning with quantitative Inductively Coupled Plasma Mass Spectrometry (ICP-MS) analysis to measure multi-element trace metal release (Ti, Al, V, Co, Cr, Cu, Zr, Fe, Ni, As, Pb) in both peri-implant sulcular fluid (PISF) and inflammatory granulation tissue, determining the specific particulate load generated by metallic curettage.
: Mechanical Debridement with Plastic Curettes — This arm utilizes implant-compatible, flexible plastic curettes adhering to identical stroke parameters (10-15 strokes per surface horizontally and apico-coronally). Its unique methodological value lies in comparing polymer-based mechanical instrumentation against metallic counterparts, specifically quantifying whether non-metallic mechanical debridement mitigates multi-element trace metal release (analyzed via ICP-MS across 11 elemental parameters in PISF and granulation tissue) while maintaining therapeutic clinical efficacy in peri-implantitis management.
: 940 nm Diode Laser Decontamination — This arm implements a laser-assisted decontamination protocol using a 940 nm diode laser operated in non-contact mode at an average power of 1 W with a 300 µm fiber tip applied for 60 seconds per surface. This intervention investigates the thermal and bactericidal efficacy of optical decontamination, uniquely pairing it with high-precision ICP-MS trace metal quantification (Ti, Al, V, Co, Cr, Cu, Zr, Fe, Ni, As, Pb) from PISF and granulation tissue samples to evaluate whether photon-based decontamination induces surface alterations or ion shedding compared to mechanical modalities.
: Submarginal Erythritol Air-Polishing and PEEK Instrumentation — This arm employs a two-step Guided Biofilm Therapy (GBT) protocol combining submarginal air-polishing with erythritol powder via a PerioFlow nozzle followed by a medical-grade PEEK (Piezon PI) instrument for hard deposit removal. This advanced combination protocol is uniquely designed to eliminate biofilm without scarring the titanium surface, its safety and efficacy rigorously validated through quantitative multi-element ICP-MS analysis of 11 trace metals in PISF and granulation tissue samples collected at baseline, 24 hours, and 6 weeks.
: Clinical Observation and Sampling Only from Healthy implants — This non-intervention control cohort comprises individuals with clinically healthy dental implants who receive no surgical or therapeutic decontamination. It serves as a vital comparative baseline for the study, allowing researchers to evaluate physiological baseline levels of multi-element trace metal concentrations (Ti, Al, V, Co, Cr, Cu, Zr, Fe, Ni, As, Pb) in PISF and tissue samples relative to diseased, treated implant sites without confounding therapeutic variables.
Link: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07811921

## NCT07818187
Effectiveness of Active Cycle of Breathing Techniques in Patients With Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease: A Randomized Controlled Trial

Intervention: : ACBT+OPEP — Participants undergo an 8-week home-based pulmonary rehabilitation program combining ACBT with O-PEP therapy. At baseline (Week 0), each participant receives individual face-to-face instruction covering the three ACBT phases - Breathing Control (BC), Thoracic Expansion Exercises (TEE), and Forced Expiration Technique (FET) - and correct use of the tube-valve O-PEP device. Competency is verified by return demonstration. A practice manual, self-monitoring diary, and instructional videos are provided. Each session follows the sequence: BC → TEE ×3 → FET, immediately followed by 10-15 O-PEP exhalations, then FET, coughing, and expectoration. Sessions are performed twice daily (≥8 hours apart), 30-60 minutes per session, for 8 weeks. Biweekly remote monitoring is conducted via LINE. Upon completion, the O-PEP device is retrieved to prevent carryover contamination.
: Usual Care (Standard Medical Care) — Participants receive standard outpatient medical care only, consisting of routine pulmonology follow-up, prescribed pharmacological management (bronchodilators and/or inhaled corticosteroids as clinically indicated), and standard respiratory health education including disease self-management, smoking cessation, pursed-lip breathing, and diaphragmatic breathing. No ACBT training, O-PEP device, or individualized airway clearance instruction is provided during this period.
Link: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07818187

SUMMARY:

The panel documents the patient's identity, personal preferences, and biographical details, making this information visible to all members of the care team. It is displayed within the patient's private Intensive Care Unit (ICU) room in a location that preserves data privacy, and is completed as part of routine clinical care. Patients in the intervention arm also receive standard ICU care as practiced at each participating unit.

: Orofacial Myofunctional Therapy — Myofunctional therapy (also called orofacial myofunctional therapy or OMT) trains muscles in your mouth and face to move as they should and rest in the proper positions. Guidance will be tailored to each participant's needs to encourage adherence to the proposed practices and changes in behaviors and lifestyle habits that may contribute to worsening tinnitus.
: Myofascial release — Myofascial release is part of the G1 intervention and will be delivered in four sessions. Myofascial trigger points will be treated using gradually increasing, sustained digital pressure until the participant reports no tenderness at the site, followed by manual techniques along the taut muscle band. Target muscles will include the infraspinatus, levator scapulae, upper trapezius, splenius capitis, splenius cervicis, sternal head of the sternocleidomastoid, superficial masseter, anterior temporalis, and lateral and medial pterygoids. Myofascial release will last 30 minutes during the first session, which will also include counseling and an introduction to mindfulness. Each of the remaining three sessions will include 40 minutes of myofascial release.
: Pilates — Pilates is part of the G1 intervention and will be delivered during the second month of treatment, comprising four weekly 40 minutes sessions at the tinnitus outpatient clinic. Mat-based exercises will use a mat, a small exercise ball, and 1-kg dumbbells, with adaptations for individuals with tinnitus, neck pain, and muscle tension. Each exercise will be performed in one set of 10, 15, or 20 repetitions, adjusted to the participant's fitness level and reported pain and fatigue. Sessions will include preparatory pre-Pilates and breathing exercises, basic exercises incorporating Pilates principles, and final stretching. Participants with temporomandibular disorders will also receive specific temporomandibular joint exercises and instructions to perform them at home once daily until the end of treatment.
: Auriculotherapy — Auriculotherapy is part of the G1 intervention and will be delivered during the third month of treatment in four weekly 10-minute sessions. Auricular points will be selected based on Traditional Chinese Medicine and previous studies addressing tinnitus and muscle tension in the cervical, thoracic, and temporomandibular regions. Mustard seeds will be secured to the ear with microporous adhesive tape, alternating between the right and left ears each week. Participants will be instructed to keep the seeds in place for up to three days and press each auricular point 15 times, at least three times daily.
: Dry Needling — Dry needling is part of the G1 intervention and will be delivered during the third month of treatment in four weekly sessions alongside auriculotherapy. Sterile, single-use, disposable acupuncture needles measuring 0.20 × 30 mm (DUX) will be used. The therapist will wear gloves, and the skin will be disinfected with 70% w/w alcohol. Participants will be positioned supine for needling of the upper trapezius, sternocleidomastoid, masseter, and lateral pterygoid; prone for the upper trapezius and infraspinatus; and side-lying for the splenius capitis, splenius cervicis, and levator scapulae.
: Relaxation Audio Recordings — This intervention is part of the G2 control group and consists of listening to relaxation recordings selected from YouTube during the first and second months of treatment. The recordings will be matched in duration to the mindfulness practices used in the G1 intervention group. Participants will be instructed to listen once daily. The recordings will be replaced weekly and sent via WhatsApp.
: Manual Manipulation Without Trigger Point Deactivation — This intervention is part of the G2 control group and will be delivered during the first month of treatment in four weekly sessions. Participants will receive manual manipulation without myofascial trigger point deactivation techniques. Session duration will match that of myofascial release in G1: 30 minutes in the first session and 40 minutes in each of the remaining three sessions.
: Gentle Movements and Stretching — This intervention is part of the G2 control group and will be delivered during the second month of treatment in four weekly 40 minutes sessions. Participants will perform gentle, unloaded movements, including upper limb, lower limb, and spinal stretching, as a comparison intervention to the Pilates exercises performed by the G1 group.
: Auricular Tape Application Without Stimulation — This intervention is part of the G2 control group and will be delivered during the third month of treatment in four weekly sessions. Microporous adhesive tape will be applied to the ear without seeds or stimulation of auricular points, as a sham comparison to auriculotherapy in the G1 group.
: Superficial Skin Needling — This intervention is part of the G2 control group and will be delivered during the third month of treatment in four weekly sessions, alongside auricular tape application without stimulation. Participants will receive superficial skin needling in the abdominal, quadriceps, and gastrocnemius regions as a comparison procedure to dry needling in the G1 group.
Link: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07941648

## NCT07942181
Passive Mechanical Stiffness Properties and Active Neuromuscular Function of the Foot and Ankle Complex Influence on Running Biomechanics

Intervention: : Incremental Running Exercise Test — An incremental treadmill test to volitional exhaustion will first be conducted. The test will start at 8 km·h-¹ with speed increasing by 1 km·h-¹ every 3 minutes. Capillary blood samples will be collected at the end of each stage to measure blood lactate concentration. Respiratory gas exchange will be continuously recorded throughout the test to determine ventilatory thresholds and maximal oxygen uptake. LT1 will be identified as the first sustained increase in blood lactate concentration above baseline values. LT2 will be determined using the modified D-max method. A third-order polynomial function will be fitted to the lactate-velocity relationship, and LT2 will be defined as the point of maximal perpendicular distance between the fitted curve and the straight line connecting the first systematic rise in blood lactate concentration and the final lactate value.
: Running Biomechanics Assessment — Participants will undergo a running biomechanics assessment on an instrumented treadmill at three individualized speeds determined from their lactate thresholds (LT1 and LT2). Running trials will be performed under shod and barefoot conditions. Three-dimensional motion capture, ground reaction forces, plantar pressure distribution, and metabolic measurements will be collected to characterize running mechanics, foot-ankle kinetics, and running economy.
: Foot-Ankle Neuromuscular Assessment — Participants will undergo a comprehensive neuromuscular assessment of the foot-ankle complex. The testing battery will include maximal voluntary isometric strength of the plantar flexors, dorsiflexors, invertors, evertors, and toe flexors; plantar flexor power; muscular endurance through a heel-rise test; and reactive muscle function through hopping and rebound jump tests. Additional countermovement and drop jump assessments will be performed to characterize lower-limb neuromuscular capacities.
Link: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07942181

## NCT07942740
Modulatory Effects of Combined TMS-tACS Stimulation on Central Autonomic Coupling and Cognitive Function

Intervention: : TMS Stimulation — Transcranial magnetic stimulation was applied to the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (DLPFC), targeting the F3 site based on the international 10-20 EEG system. Repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) was delivered at a frequency of 10 Hz with an intensity of 80% of the resting motor threshold (RMT). The stimulation protocol consisted of 30-second stimulation periods followed by 30-second inter-train intervals, with 15 repeated stimulation cycles and a total of 4,500 pulses. No concurrent tACS stimulation was applied during this condition.
: tACS Stimulation — Transcranial alternating current stimulation (tACS) was applied to the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (DLPFC), targeting the F3 site according to the international 10-20 EEG system. The stimulation intensity was set at 1 mA and continuously delivered for 15 minutes, including 5-second ramp-up and ramp-down periods. No concurrent transcranial magnetic stimulation was applied during this condition.
: TMS-tACS Combined Stimulation — Combined transcranial magnetic stimulation and transcranial alternating current stimulation (TMS-tACS) were applied to the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (DLPFC) targeting the F3 site according to the international 10-20 EEG system. Repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) was delivered at a frequency of 10 Hz with an intensity of 80% of the resting motor threshold (RMT). The stimulation protocol consisted of 30-second stimulation periods followed by 30-second intervals, with 15 repeated stimulation cycles and a total of 4,500 pulses. Transcranial alternating current stimulation (tACS) was applied simultaneously with an intensity of 1 mA for 15 minutes, including 5-second ramp-up and ramp-down periods. During combined stimulation, TMS pulses were triggered at the peak phase of the tACS sinusoidal waveform to achieve phase-synchronized neuromodulation.
: Sham TMS-tACS Stimulation — A sham stimulation condition was applied to simulate the sensory experience of active TMS-tACS stimulation without delivering effective neuromodulation. During sham tACS, electrical current was briefly delivered at the beginning of stimulation to mimic the initial skin sensation, while sham TMS was performed using prerecorded stimulation sounds to reproduce the auditory experience associated with active stimulation. No effective magnetic or electrical stimulation was delivered.
Link: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07942740

: Mediterranean Diet Education — Participants will take part in a 12 week nutritional intervention, followed by a 12 month follow-up period. The program includes 14 weekly group education sessions and one 30-minute individual consultation. Group sessions cover healthy eating principles, Mediterranean diet, intuitive eating, meal planning, hunger and satiety awareness, emotional triggers, mindful eating, real-life nutrition situations, motivation, and strategies for maintaining healthy habits. The individual consultation addresses personal challenges and tailors dietary guidance to the participant's lifestyle and health status. Dietary intake is monitored using structured 24-hour recalls at multiple time points throughout the intervention and follow-up periods.Participants will wear smart bracelets to monitor physical activity, heart rate, and sleep to track their daily routine and progress.
: Behavioral: Stress-Resilience Training — Participants will take part in a 12-week program focused on strengthening psychological resilience and stress management. The program includes workshops and group support sessions to encourage experience sharing and motivation, with additional online and telephone support. Participants will wear smart bracelets to monitor physical activity, heart rate, and sleep to track their daily routine and progress.

## NCT07314957
The Role of Lifestyle in Maintaining Health: Biological, Psychological and Social Responses of the Organism to Lifestyle

Intervention: : Intervention of physical activity — The intervention combines supervised physical activity (2 times a week for 12 weeks) with the use of a smart bracelet to continuously monitor heart rate, steps and hours of sleep. The intervention aims to reduce sedentary behavior and improve metabolic, oxidative and psychological health in adults with overweight or obesity.
: Mediterranean Diet Education — Participants will take part in a 12 week nutritional intervention, followed by a 12 month follow-up period. The program includes 14 weekly group education sessions and one 30-minute individual consultation. Group sessions cover healthy eating principles, Mediterranean diet, intuitive eating, meal planning, hunger and satiety awareness, emotional triggers, mindful eating, real-life nutrition situations, motivation, and strategies for maintaining healthy habits. The individual consultation addresses personal challenges and tailors dietary guidance to the participant's lifestyle and health status. Dietary intake is monitored using structured 24-hour recalls at multiple time points throughout the intervention and follow-up periods.Participants will wear smart bracelets to monitor physical activity, heart rate, and sleep to track their daily routine and progress.
: Behavioral: Stress-Resilience Training — Participants will take part in a 12-week program focused on strengthening psychological resilience and stress management. The program includes workshops and group support sessions to encourage experience sharing and motivation, with additional online and telephone support. Participants will wear smart bracelets to monitor physical activity, heart rate, and sleep to track their daily routine and progress.

Participants will be instructed to retain the instilled solution in the bladder for an appropriate period to allow sufficient contact with the bladder mucosa. The treatment will be administered once weekly for 4 consecutive weeks. Clinical symptoms, including urinary frequency, urgency, dysuria, hematuria, and treatment-related adverse events, will be monitored during treatment and follow-up.
: Sodium Hyaluronate (Hyalein) — Participants in this group will receive intravesical instillation of sodium hyaluronate (Hyalein) once weekly for 4 consecutive weeks. Clinical symptoms and treatment-related adverse events will be monitored during treatment and follow-up.
: Normal Saline (0.9% NaCl) — Participants will receive intravesical instillation of normal saline (0.9% NaCl). After bladder emptying, a predefined volume of normal saline will be slowly instilled into the bladder through a sterile urinary catheter and retained for an appropriate period. The treatment will be administered once weekly for 4 consecutive weeks. Clinical symptoms and adverse events will be monitored during treatment and follow-up.

## NCT07777939
Continuous 24-Hour Transcutaneous Electrical Nerve Stimulation for Post-Cesarean Pain Management: A Randomized Controlled Trial

Intervention: : TENS — Participants randomized to the intervention group will receive TENS in addition to standard postoperative analgesia. TENS will be initiated within 2 hours after cesarean delivery and administered during the first 24 postoperative hours. Participants will be instructed to wear the device continuously during this period.

Each TENS stimulation cycle will last 1 hour, using a frequency of 80 Hz, a pulse width of 200 µs, and an intensity of 20-40 mA. Participants will be encouraged to restart the stimulation program at the end of each hourly cycle for up to 24 hours. Stimulation may be temporarily discontinued in the event of discomfort or skin irritation, during mobilization or hygiene activities, or at the participant's request.

All participants will additionally receive the institution's standard postoperative care and analgesic regimen following cesarean delivery.

Intervention: : Rhaeos Shunt Monitoring System (RSMS) — The Rhaeos Shunt Monitoring System (RSMS) is an investigational, wireless, noninvasive thermal flow detection device that is applied to the skin overlying an implanted cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) shunt. The device uses controlled thermal energy and temperature sensors to detect thermal patterns associated with CSF flow. Measurements are obtained using a tablet application, and device results are encoded to maintain blinding. The device is used for research purposes only and is not used to guide clinical care.
: ShuntCheck III — ShuntCheck III is an FDA-cleared, noninvasive thermal flow detection device used as the predicate comparator. The device uses transcutaneous thermal dilution produced by an instant cold pack and a disposable thermosensor array applied over the implanted CSF shunt to detect shunt flow. Measurements are obtained using the manufacturer's software, and results are encoded to maintain blinding. The device is used for comparison with the investigational device and is not used to guide clinical care during the study.

## NCT07837141
Noninvasive High Frequency Oscillatory Ventilation Versus Nasal Intermittent Mandatory Ventilation as Primary Respiratory Support in Preterm Neonates With Respiratory Distress Syndrome: A Non Inferiority Randomized Controlled Trial

Intervention: : Noninvasive High Frequency Oscillatory Ventilation — Noninvasive high frequency oscillatory ventilation will be delivered as primary respiratory support through a nasal interface using a RAM cannula or Infant Flow Generator and an nHFOV capable ventilator. Initial settings will include mean airway pressure of 10-12 cmH₂O, amplitude of 15-25 cmH₂O, frequency of 8-12 Hz, and an inspiratory to expiratory ratio of 1:1. Mean airway pressure may be increased by 1 cmH₂O to a maximum of 20 cmH₂O, and amplitude may be increased by 5 cmH₂O to a maximum of 35 cmH₂O. Settings will be adjusted according to clinical response to maintain SpO₂ between 90% and 95%.
: Nasal Intermittent Mandatory Ventilation — Nasal intermittent mandatory ventilation will be delivered as primary respiratory support through a nasal interface using a RAM cannula or Infant Flow Generator and an NIMV capable ventilator. Initial settings will include PEEP of 8-12 cmH₂O, peak inspiratory pressure of 18-24 cmH₂O, inspiratory time of 0.5 seconds, and respiratory rate of 30 breaths per minute. The respiratory rate may be increased by 5 breaths per minute to a maximum of 50 breaths per minute based on PaCO₂. FiO₂ and other ventilator settings may be adjusted according to clinical response to maintain SpO₂ between 90% and 95%.
Link: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07837141

Intervention: : Drug-coated balloon-based intervention — In the DCB-based PCI group, lesion preparation may include conventional, non-compliant, cutting, or scoring balloons and, when needed, other calcium-modification techniques. An adequately prepared lesion has expansion with a balloon-to-vessel diameter ratio of at least 0.90, residual diameter stenosis of 30% or less, TIMI grade 3 flow, and no flow-limiting dissection or risk of vessel closure. When these conditions are met, the operator will use a paclitaxel-coated DCB (SeQuent Please NEO), sized approximately 1:1 to the reference vessel and covering the prepared segment. DCB delivery within 30 seconds and inflation for 30-60 seconds are recommended when clinically tolerated. DES implantation is permitted for inadequate flow, residual stenosis greater than 30%, substantial recoil, a major dissection, or another procedural reason requiring immediate stenting. Such stenting is part of the assigned DCB-based strategy, not a treatment crossover.
: Drug-eluting stent-based intervention — In the DES-only PCI group, the target or culprit lesion will be treated with a contemporary newer-generation DES according to clinical practice.

Participants can participate in-person or online, and either an in-person or online group format will then be offered. As such, those who are not able to participate in the current iteration of the group will be placed on a waitlist. Screened participants who are willing to participate in the current format will be randomized into those receiving treatment immediately or in 6 months (waitlist control group).

Both parent and youth sessions will be 50- to 60-minutes long and will be administered in-person or over Zoom.

## NCT07873619
Histotripsy for Peritoneal Tumour and Lymph Node: a Pilot Study

Intervention: : Histotripsy — Histotripsy is a promising non-invasive technique that uses high-intensity ultrasound waves to disrupt tissue without damaging surrounding structures. It works by using high-intensity ultrasound waves to create microscopic bubbles within the tumour tissue. These bubbles rapidly expand and collapse, generating shock waves that disrupt the tissue. The technique is highly precise and can be targeted to specific areas of the liver, allowing for selective destruction of tumour cells while minimizing damage to healthy tissue.

## NCT07880496
The Effect of Shotblockers on Pain, Anxiety, and Cortisol Level Symptoms During Lumbar Puncture: A Randomized Controlled Study

Intervention: : Intervention Group — Patients will receive routine monitoring, pharmacological treatment, and nursing care. Under aseptic precautions, lumbar puncture will be performed in all groups using a 25-gauge Quincke spinal needle at the L3-L4 or L4-L5 intervertebral space, with patients in the lateral position. In the ShotBlocker group, after skin preparation and draping, the sterilized ShotBlocker will be placed at the puncture site and firmly pressed for 10 seconds with the non-dominant hand. The spinal needle will then pass through its slit. Methylprednisolone and bupivacaine hydrochloride will be administered into the epidural space. Saliva samples will be collected before and after the procedure for cortisol measurement. Pain and anxiety will be assessed before and 10 minutes after lumbar puncture. The procedure will be performed by the same physician in all groups.
: Control — In our research, the "Personal Information Form" will be applied to the control group patients without any intervention other than the clinical protocol. "Visual Analog Scale" and "State Anxiety Scale" will be applied to the patients 10 minutes before the lumbar puncture procedure. Saliva samples will be collected from patients before and after the lumbar puncture, and the collected samples will be stored under appropriate laboratory conditions for measurement of cortisol level. 10 minutes after the procedure is completed, the pain and anxiety levels experienced will be re-evaluated with scales.
Link: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07880496

Intervention: : Exploring Trauma Plus (ET+): A Brief Intervention for Men and Gender-Diverse Populations (Covington & Rodriguez, 2016, rev. 2021) — ET+ is an evidence-based 6-session brief intervention with a focus on trauma and PTSD, and techniques for Restorative Justice work with men (and those who identify as men). The rigorously evaluated manualized curriculum is designed for trauma treatment while emphasizing Restorative Justice principles and objectives, e.g., understanding victim impact, personal accountability, and restitution. The intervention is delivered to small groups of 10-12 men and co-led by two specially trained Peer Facilitators. Using a closed group model creates the experience of a prosocial support system based on a new value system and group agreements. This is strengthened by using Peer Facilitators as role models. The group process helps develop empathy and connectedness for other group members.

## NCT07946510
Mini-RISK in Agder: A Cluster Randomized Controlled Trial of a Low-Threshold School-Based Program for Anxious Students Delivered by School Personnel in the School Setting

Intervention: : Mini-RISK School-based group CBT — Manualized, low-threshold group CBT program for anxious youth, developed at the Department of Child and Adolescent Mental Health, Sørlandet Hospital, as a brief school-based version of the RISK multi-family exposure program. Unlike most CBT programs delivered by health professionals only, Mini-RISK is co-led by school health and school staff (a school nurse and a school social teacher) and actively involves parents and contact teachers. Youth attend sessions 2 to 8, parents sessions 1, 4, 6 and 8, and teachers sessions 1 and 8. Most session time is used for in-session exposure. Parents help each other's children during group exposure, and parents and teachers learn to reduce accommodation and to support exposure at home and at school. Group leaders receive ongoing supervision from experienced RISK therapists and Mini-RISK leaders.
: Usual School Nurse Support — Individual support from the public school nurse as routinely provided in Norwegian schools to students who seek help for anxiety. Content and frequency are determined by the school nurse according to need and may include supportive counseling, needs assessment, school adjustments, contact with parents and teachers, and referral to other services. Not manualized, time-limited or anxiety-specific. Quality assurance is the responsibility of each school and municipality.

Mystical Experiences Without Psychedelics: The Nature of Peak Spiritual Experiences and How Integration Leads to Human Flourishing

Intervention: : Guided Invocation for Mystical Experience — Participants will complete a single, in-person Guided Invocation for Mystical Experience (GIME) session conducted by a trained practitioner using a standardized protocol. The session includes an initial briefing and rapport-building period, followed by a structured breathing exercise (approximately 8 minutes) designed to facilitate a non-ordinary state of consciousness. Participants then receive guided imagery and verbal suggestions intended to promote relaxation, absorption, and experiential openness. The practitioner delivers a standardized script targeting features commonly associated with mystical-type experiences (e.g., unity, positive affect, and altered perception of time and space). The session includes a brief period of silent introspection, followed by re-alerting procedures. The total session duration is approximately 60 minutes.

## NCT07405658
Clinical Study on an Artificial Intelligence-Assisted Chest Radiograph Model Based on Big Data and Deep Learning for Early Detection of Kawasaki Disease

Intervention: : AI-Based Early Warning System for Kawasaki Disease — This study utilizes an AI-based early warning system for Kawasaki Disease (KD) to predict the optimal IVIG treatment window and assess coronary risk. The system analyzes chest X-ray (CXR) images and integrates them with clinical data such as CRP levels and clinical symptoms. The intervention involves the development of a multi-modal dynamic prediction model that uses a dual-pathway convolutional neural network (CNN) to extract relevant CXR features and a graph neural network to integrate laboratory indicators. The AI system outputs a prediction of the IVIG treatment window and estimates the risk of coronary artery damage. This early warning system aims to reduce diagnosis time and improve treatment outcomes by identifying high-risk KD patients earlier, enabling timely intervention and personalized treatment plans. The model is designed to be lightweight (under 50MB) to be easily applicable in primary care settings.
Link: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07405658

SUMMARY:

Level 3 From the end position of level 1, the participant slowly lowered one leg such that the heel reached approximate 12cm above the ground. Then the leg slid out to fully extend the knee.

Level 4 From the final position of level 1, the participant slowly lowered both legs together such that the heels contacted the plinth. Then the legs slid out to fully extend the knees.

2. Side plank The patient lying on the side supported on his elbow and hip, knees bent to 90 degrees, free hand place on the opposite shoulder. If patient not able to perform side support exercise, the patient would assume the side lying position and initiate the contraction of quadratus lumborum by trying to lift both lower limbs up toward the ceiling.

## NCT07672535
Comparison of the Effects of High-Intensity and Low-Intensity Inspiratory Muscle Training in Individuals With Multiple Sclerosis

Intervention: : High intensity interval IMT — Participants with multiple sclerosis (MS) in this group will perform high intensity interval inspiratory muscle training (IMT) for 8 weeks, three times per week (one supervised by a physiotherapist and two home-based sessions). The protocol consists of 7 cycles of 2 minutes of exercise followed by 1 minute of rest, with each session lasting 21 minutes. Training intensity will start at 30% of maximal inspiratory pressure (MIP) and progressively increase to 70% by the third week. From week 4 onward, intensity will be maintained at 70% of MIP and adjusted according to tolerance, based on a Borg scale rating of 3-5.

In addition, participants in this group will receive a conventional rehabilitation program for 8 weeks, consisting of three sessions per week: one supervised session conducted by a physiotherapist and two supervised home-based sessions.
: Low intensity IMT — Participants with multiple sclerosis (MS) in this group will perform low intensity inspiratory muscle training (IMT) for 8 weeks, consisting of five sessions per week: one supervised by a physiotherapist and four home-based supervised sessions. The training will be performed as two daily sessions of 15 minutes each, totaling 30 minutes per day. Low intensity IMT will be conducted at 30% of maximal inspiratory pressure (MIP). Training intensity will be reassessed and adjusted to 30% of MIP every two weeks during supervised sessions, based on repeated MIP measurements. During training, participants will be instructed to maintain a seated position with the upper chest and shoulders in a relaxed posture.

In addition, participants in this group will receive a conventional rehabilitation program for 8 weeks, consisting of three sessions per week: one supervised session conducted by a physiotherapist and two supervised home-based sessions.
: Conventional rehabilitation — Participants in this group will undergo a conventional rehabilitation program for 8 weeks, consisting of three sessions per week: one supervised by a physiotherapist and two home-based supervised sessions. Each session will last approximately 40 minutes. The program will include warm-up exercises, aerobic exercises, strengthening exercises, balance exercises, and cool-down exercises.
Link: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07672535

## NCT07758647
NO-Meal Announcement in Automated Insulin Delivery (Open-source and Commercial) Systems

Intervention: : Open-Source Automated Insulin Delivery (OS-AID) — Participants will use their own OS-AID system, including Loop, AndroidAPS, or OpenAPS, in combination with a compatible insulin pump and Dexcom G6 or Dexcom G7 continuous glucose monitoring (CGM). These systems use open-source algorithms to automatically adjust insulin delivery based on real-time CGM data through adaptive basal insulin modulation and, depending on the platform, automated correction boluses. Participants will continue using their established OS-AID settings throughout the intervention period without software updates and will be asked to perform two unannounced meal-challenges.
: Commercial Automated Insulin Delivery (C-AID) — Participants will use a commercially available hybrid closed-loop AID system compatible with Dexcom G6 or Dexcom G7 CGM. Depending on study allocation and participants' usual device, the commercial system will include Tandem t X2 with Control-IQ technology or Omnipod 5. Participants not already using a compatible commercial AID system will receive study equipment and standardized training before initiating the intervention. Commercial AID systems automatically adjust insulin delivery based on continuous glucose measurements using manufacturer-specific algorithms while continuing to recommend user-initiated meal announcements and boluses for optimal performance.

## NCT07776652
The Effect of Postural Biofeedback on Disease Activity and Pain in Individuals With Axial Spondyloarthritis

Intervention: : Standard Exercise Program — Participants in both study groups will receive a standard exercise program for 8 weeks, with two physiotherapist-supervised sessions per week and approximately 45 minutes per session. The program will include warm-up, spinal mobility exercises, stretching exercises, postural exercises, trunk stabilization exercises, lower extremity strengthening exercises, breathing exercises, and cool-down. Exercises will be performed at moderate intensity according to the participant's clinical condition and exercise tolerance. Set number, repetitions, and resistance will be progressively increased by the physiotherapist according to individual performance.
: Wearable Postural Biofeedback — Participants in the intervention group will additionally use a wearable postural biofeedback device (Kodgem Straight™, Türkiye) for 8 weeks. The device uses inertial sensors to monitor the position of the upper thoracic region in real time and provides vibrotactile feedback when a predefined postural threshold is exceeded. The device will be individually calibrated before use. Participants will be instructed to use the device three days per week for at least 3 hours per day during activities requiring prolonged static posture, such as desk work, computer use, meal preparation, or ironing. Device adherence will be monitored and recorded by the researcher.
Link: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07776652

## NCT07937228
Objective Assessment of Sensory Block Level During Spinal Anesthesia Using Segmental Near-Infrared Spectroscopy: A Prospective Observational Study

Intervention: : Segmental Near-Infrared Spectroscopy (NIRS) Monitoring — Segmental near-infrared spectroscopy (NIRS) will be used to noninvasively measure regional tissue oxygen saturation (StO₂) at the T10 and T4 dermatomal levels in patients undergoing spinal anesthesia.

Measurements will be obtained before spinal anesthesia and at 0, 5, 10, 15, 20, and 30 minutes following intrathecal injection.

Changes in T10 tissue oxygen saturation will be evaluated for their ability to identify sensory blockade reaching T10 or higher, while T4 measurements will be assessed for their association with further cephalad block spread.

NIRS-derived parameters will be compared with standard clinical sensory block assessments. NIRS measurements will be collected for observational research purposes and will not guide anesthetic management.
Link: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07937228

## NCT07950358
A Single-Center, Randomized Controlled Trial of Transcoronary Radiofrequency Ablation Versus Transcoronary Alcohol Ablation for Hypertrophic Obstructive Cardiomyopathy

Intervention: : transcoronary radiofrequency ablation — Both groups received SonoVue injection into the septal branch, and transthoracic echocardiography was used to confirm that the ablation site was the critical lesion responsible for obstruction. In the TCRFA group, a microcatheter was advanced over a coronary guidewire into the septal branch; the proximal end of the guidewire was connected to a radiofrequency ablation generator, and myocardial ablation was delivered around the guidewire tip. The ablation power was set at 30-40 W, with three applications of 30 seconds each at a single target site. Intraoperatively, electrocardiogram, heart rate, blood pressure and symptoms were closely monitored in both groups, and the left ventricular outflow tract gradient (LVOTG) was measured in real time via catheter and ultrasound. For patients in the TCRFA group whose post-treatment LVOTG failed to meet the criteria for obstruction relief, supplementary endocardial ablation would be performed intraoperatively to achieve the target reduction of LVOT
: transcoronary alcohol ablation — SonoVue is injected into the septal branch, and transthoracic echocardiography is used to confirm that the ablation site is the critical site causing obstruction. In the ASA group, 2-3 mL of absolute alcohol is injected into the septal branch. Intraoperatively, the patient's electrocardiogram, heart rate, blood pressure and symptoms are closely monitored, and LVOTG is measured in real time using catheters and ultrasound.
Link: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07950358

SUMMARY:

## NCT00018057
Study of Neuro-Cognitive Correlates of Pediatric Anxiety Disorders

Intervention: : Attention Bias Modification Training — The intervention is computer-based. The active and control treatments have two components. In one component of the active intervention, subjects are asked to indicate the identity of a letter that appears behind a neutral face, opposite from an angry face. In another component of the active intervention, subjects are asked to identify numbers that are hidden within a puzzle, in locations distal from angry faces. In both components of the active intervention, subjects implicitly learn to shift their attention away from angry faces. This is because the faces are systematically arranged to be far removed from letters and numbers that need to be identified. The control arm of the intervention involves similar components. However, unlike in the intervention arm, angry faces appear in various locations near letters and numbers. Therefore, attention is not shaped in the control arm. This intervention requires five minutes per session and is administered before weekly psychotherapy sessions.
: Fluoxetine — Randomized assignment.
: Cognitive Behavioral Therapy
Link: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT00018057
